Analyze this product review:

If you're an iPhone user but don't really care for the techy, gadgety look of the Apple Watch, The Amazfit Active series is a good alternative. It's lightweight, it's a slim, timeless design (no pun intended) and uses standard, easily swappable watch bands. It's a classic look that I enjoy.
I purchased the Active 2 Premium Round, which comes with 2 bands: a leather band and a silicone band, and allegedly has sapphire glass instead of tempered.
Now, this watch is first and foremost a fitness tracker. As I am not a whey protein guzzling gym bro, I cannot speak about the fitness features with much authority. The thing throws words at me like HYROX, VO2 MAX, Hybrid Charge, and my eyes just glaze over. There are plenty (maybe too many) YouTube videos that explain all that, but I'll stick to the features I actually use and understand.
Pros:
The battery lasts for DAYS on a single charge. Maybe over a full week if you keep the brightness lower. So with the longer battery life (unlike some watches), you can actually use the sleep tracking feature!
There is an always-on display option, but it cuts your battery life to about 2 days in my experience.
The screen is bright and colorful. It's not the brightest on the market, but sufficient. Good contrast.
The "raise to view" function works every time. (I've had watches previously that would fail at this basic function.)
Phone notifications come through instantly.
You can take calls on your watch. Not really something I care about, but I suppose it's a good feature to have.
All your health telemetry syncs with Apple Health app, so step count, heart rate, sleep quality, and much more shows up as expected.
The watch autodetects workouts and syncs with other Fitness apps like Strava. I'm a cyclist and use Strava to track rides, and to my surprise, it populates your activities into Strava with little to no interaction required.
The somewhat smaller 44mm watch face doesn't look completely stupid on my smaller wrists. I'm a male, but not every male has tree trunk arms, and this size watch fits me perfectly.
Cons:
You cannot reply to text messages on iPhone. That's not Amazfit's fault, that's just Apple's walled garden. But don't be fooled. I've seen posts saying there are workarounds - there are not. You CAN use a third party app to reply to FACEBOOK or WHATSAPP messages, but there is nothing that works specifically with Apple's Messages app.
The UI could use some improvements and polish, and some of the controls are inconsistent. What I would call the "home" button does not work universally in all apps which can make navigating menus and apps a bit confusing.
This model does not have wifi. So syncing data (apps, watch faces, etc) is done over Bluetooth so it does take much longer.
There is a built-in AI assistant. I do not use it nor want it. I would prefer if there was an option to disable it completely. It isn't too intrusive, but it does show up on notifications.
Conclusion:
Is it a 1:1 replacement for the functionality of the Apple Watch? No.. Does it supply enough functionality to replace the Apple watch to my personal satisfaction? Yes. And for the price, the Amazfit brand is probably the absolute best value watch on the market. I recommend the watch if you fall into the slender category of people that prefer iPhone but also prefer an alternative to the (subjectively) ugly Apple Watch. And if you happen to also appreciate the plethora of fitness tracking features, well that's just gravy.

I was surprised to find I actually love this watch. I’ve got a modest watch collection of Hamiltons, Seikos and Orients but the Amazfit has become my daily wearer. The size is perfect and it’s super comfortable because of its light weight. It also doesn’t look cheap—physical quality is way beyond its price. In terms of battery I turn off the sleep tracking and HR monitoring because I just don’t use it. With those two settings off (and AOD off) I get 7-10 days of battery, basically just using it as a smart watch. I am a cyclist and have used it for recording rides—it does this well, but the GPS battery drain is high. Maybe 20-25% for a 90 minute ride. Surprisingly when took it for a long backpacking weekend the battery did much better. For three 6 hour hikes, the battery drained about 40% each. That was better than I expected, and included using the mapping/route features along with HR data. Speaking of routes, the backpacking and cycling routes worked surprisingly very very well, with the maps sharp and crisp and spot on with the trails in front of me, as well as intersecting trails. I was honestly very surprised of the watches ability in this area. In terms of battery life I did have to recharge overnight just to be safe, while backpacking, but no more so than my Garmin Instinct (the first gen model). And the HR data on the Amazfit is much more accurate while backpacking than my Garmin. In terms of GPS functionality, on my bike rides in the suburbs, it performs flawlessly. My ride data perfectly matches the curvature of streets and mileage is accurate when compared to my Wahoo bike computer or Strava data. While backpacking in the mountains with lots of tree cover, cliff faces, tall mountains etc. it was less accurate, with the gps plot wandering off trail occasionally for long bits. However, this did not significantly affect my mileage data—it just made my route data less “pretty” when analyzing after the fact. Lastly, the altitude data is not great. Sometimes it worked really well over the course of a six hour mountain hike, other times it was off by a good 1200 feet over a course with 4000 ft of gain. So if the altimeter accuracy is a must for you, this is probably not your watch. Apps like Strava can automatically correct altitude data when you upload (as can the Zepp app) so I don’t consider this a deal killer.
Bottom line—are there better fitness watches that provide higher accuracy and battery life for what I use the watch for (cycling, backpacking) — YES. My Wahoo bike computer is way better in every respect. But it also cost $350. And I’m sure a Garmin Fenix would kill this thing in terms of backpacking data and accuracy, at the cost of $600-$700. BUT, for $100 this little watch does amazingly well with routes, mapping, HR data, GPS tracking etc, and for day to day use (basic smart watch features) I love it. For $100 I’ll keep using it until it dies or until I simply get bored with it and want something else. The value is simply too great to not keep it and use the hell out of it.

One of the most comfortable and tunable chairs I've used. I am 6ft1, 210lbs. I happened to try it out at a friend's house and insisted they send me a link!
Finding the instructions in the box was a bit frustrating. They were inside of the plastic covering the seat of the chair, instead of just loosely packed in the box. Having already read complaints about missing instructions, I immediately feared I was one of the victims, until I got half way though the assembly and turned the seat over to notice them stuck in there.
I would have searched more diligently if not for the reviews. But it all worked out in the end.
This is the first cloth seated office chair I have ever purchased. I wish they had scotchguarded it. Minus 1 star.
On day 5, a full cup of coffee was attacked by a large bag of chips and went flying off the table when I had my back turned!
You can't make this stuff up!
The seat absorbed it like a sponge. I had even thought to Scotchguard it the previous evening, and was too lazy to follow through. So...Scotchguard this ASAP when you get it!
The cloth seat is more comfortable than my previous leather and pleather chairs that cost the same or more. Also, I'm not building up as much heat in the seat.
The arm rests are not perfect. The adjustment is okay. But there is a sharp edge where the bottom and top half of the outer shell was formed. It can almost cut your hand and detracts from the comfort of the chair when you hit that edge or grip the armrest as you are sitting down or getting up.
The armrests seem adequate at present but they are about 35% thinner than the armrests on my old chair, of similar composition. I'm not confident they will hold up and be comfortable over the long term.
Another caveat about this type of armrest shell, is that the plastic tends to crack over time from your elbows and arms digging into it, along with body oils that seem to attack the the pleather surface. When that happens, it pinches your arm when used. That was the main reason for replacing my older chair. I hope this one may have some better results. Time will tell.
The mesh back is comfortable and allows my skin to breath. I really love being able to adjust the recline position to more than one angle! It's usually all or nothing.
The adjustments on the lumbar and headrest are useful and comfortable .
The chair doesn't raise up as high as my old chair, but it is adequate, barely.
Overall, I would give the chair 4 stars so far and would buy it again.
I may try to trim the sharp edge on the armrest. The left one seems to be the real problem. The right armrest seems better formed near the front edge where I notice it most. The right armrest has the sharper edge toward the back where I don't contact it often.

I've been looking for a new chair to replace a cheap $30 chair i bought off of Amazon last year that had been killing my back and shoulders. I wanted something in the $150-$200 range and settled on the M18. Shipping was a fast 3 days with Prime and the box arrived in great condition.
All parts were separately wrapped or in their own boxes. Came with all hardware and nothing was missing. Assembly took me a little longer then normal because i have rotator cuff injury in my left shoulder so that arm is mostly useless. The most difficult part for me was attaching the wheels to the base. Other then that it was simple.
Once the chair was assembled i sat in it for the first time and started making my adjustments with the recline feature, armrest level along with the headrest. Next i reached around for the lumbar support knob and tried to adjust it but with my bad shoulder i decided to just get out of the seat and turn it around and adjust it with both hands. After spinning the chair a round to get at the lumbar knob i noticed a large crack in the plastic in the middle of the back of the lumbar plastic piece. I had not made any lumbar adjustments yet so i assumed this is how i received it. The lumbar support comes preinstalled to the backrest so it either was damaged before or during the shipping process. Either way it was damaged before being delivered to me. The lumbar support still functioned properly but it was still broken.
I decided to contact Sihoo's customer support that came along with the installation instructions regarding the damaged lumbar piece. I received a reply the next day and after sending them some more info about my order and a couple pics they shipped me a replacement part which took a week to arrive. I swapped out the damaged part and after owning the chair for a week so far i am really happy with my purchase.
Im about 5'10 180lbs. At its highest height level my feet reach the ground comfortably flat footed. The backrest fully covers my back and the headrest adjusts very well to sit on the back of my lower head/upper neck. The armrests only go up and down....not forward and back or tilt inwards. This is fine for me as they are grooved to fit your forearm while sitting at your desk/keyboard. The armrests are also a soft cushioned rubber material...not a hard plastic. The mesh of the backrest and headrest are good material and seem well made. The seat is very wide and the cushioning is firm which i prefer. Usually more firm cushioning seems to last longer and hold its form. The base of the chair is VERY sturdy and made of all metal. My chair is on carpet and holds its position very well. As far as recline goes you can set it to recline all the way back, half way or lock the chair in the upright position. You can also adjust the resistance on the reclining feature.
So that being said im very happy with my purchase. It arrived with a slight flaw which the company corrected in a fast manor and was very polite in their customer support. I personally don't have a lot of experience with many office chairs and have never used a high end chair($500-$1000+) chair before to make any comparisons. All my chairs for the most part have been from local stores like Staples or Office Depot. Id recommend this over anything they carry in this price range....and i went and looked at their products before buying this chair as well.

No matter what I did, the volume would go back to zero and I couldn't use the headphones at all. So finally I decided to get wireless headphones, even though I once heard it's like the equivalent of putting a microwave in each of your ears. Oh well, it's 2026 and wifi and 5G and whatever else is all over the place. But then I had to go down the rabbit hole of finding headphones that were worth it. I didn't want super expensive or fancy wireless headphones for listening to music with my phone. I have over-ear Sony headphones that I use for recording and sound editing, I just really needed something to listen to music on my phone with while going for a walk. Reading reviews was frustrating and took me all over the place. Finally I decided to go with my gut and just order these. They're fine. I'm a bit of a sound snob and I need bass. These are fine. They fit well enough and comfortable enough in my ears. They don't get as loud as I would prefer, but that's probably a good thing. The bass is decent. The overall sound feels balanced for the most part. They hold a charge for a long time, too. I've only charged the case once since I bought them a couple months ago and I don't even know if they were close to needing a charge. I only really use them when I go for a walk around the neighborhood. I use them to listen to music and have not tried to use them for a call or anything. They seem easy to use, though admittedly I don't care to be bothered to learn what all the various tap combinations do. I put them in my ears, they automatically pair with my phone after the initial pairing, and I use the controls on my phone for volume and track changes. This works for me. They are fine. I do not think ANY wireless headphones have the sound quality of wired headphones, so these are fine. The sound is fine. I'm not like, "oh wow! these are amazing!" but I am happily listening to tunes as the soundtrack to my walks. I like how they fit in the case and its easy enough to throw them in my purse. I almost dropped one once, and I did not like that feeling of not being able to catch them with a cord but, that's me. I will say it is nice not to have to deal with the cord in terms of it being in the way while walking around or getting tangled in a purse. I have no idea about the water resistance because that's not something I deal with while wearing headphones. In terms of noise cancellation... it's not something I've really noticed, but now that I think about it I don't really notice the sound of the traffic/cars on the street while I am walking. This may or may not be a good thing. But I am happy with them. For the price, I am happy with them. For the sound, I am happy with them. For the purpose of walking while listening to music, I am happy with them. If you are also going down the rabbit hole of reviews trying to find basic earbuds for music listening purposes, I do suggest getting these and saving yourself any more frustration. They're not perfect, they're not incredible, but they are just fine.

Excellent monitor, but a little too saturated on default settings out of the box. For the best experience, either use sRGB mode with low local dimming at 75% or 100% brightness, or, like I do, and use DCI-P3 color mode with low local dimming at 100% brightness, and it looks really accurate and great!
As for HDR, it's a mixed bag. In order to get the best brightness and bang for your buck, you shouldn't be using this monitor with Windows HDR or macOS. If you want true 1:1 HDR, it is much better with a console that has proper HDR settings and out of the box tuning. But if you want to use it with a PC or Mac, it is still mostly fine, but I would calibrate the HDR using the built-in calibration in Windows.
The refresh rate is also a mixed bag. If your computers GPU or console doesn't support the latest DP 1.4 and/or HDMI 2.1 standard, then you won't be able to do more than 120Hz at 4K without display compression, and it looks and feels horrible when compression is on and visable at 160hz.
My recommendation is this setup for PC:
Use the DCI-P3 color mode for the best color accuracy across HDR and SDR, but if you don't plan on using HDR and use exclusively SDR, then stick to sRGB mode for the best accuracy for SDR content and gaming.
100% brightness for the best brightness and hitting the advertised HDR brightness claims. Note this may be too much for the average person, so if that's the case, stick to 75%, which still hits a respectable brightness. For HDR calibration in Windows: set to 1930 nits (small window) and 1600 nits (full screen), as those are the official rated numbers. Use exclusively 120Hz at 4K and the standard preset for overdrive, as any other preset has overshoot and ghosting and any refresh rate above 120hz is pointless if you get display compression and not that noticable or helps much in gaming.
As for the 320Hz dual-mode operation, it does not support native scaling, so you just get a blown-up 1080p image with no scaling, and it looks very blurry and unclear on the 4K display. It does hit its advertised 320Hz, but it is unusable in my opinion due to the blurriness of the picture from the lack of proper image display scaling. I also think they are slightly overdriving the pixels more than usual because even on the standard preset, there is still a lot of visible ghosting and overshoot on the monitor. I had to fully turn it off to get rid of it, but that defeats the point of the 320Hz mode, as it introduces more input delay for a clearer, smoother image. If you bought this monitor purely for the 320Hz mode and don’t plan to use 4K, you would be better off with a monitor that has native 320Hz support. This is clearly more of a 4K monitor than a 320Hz 1080p one.
In conclusion, if you are looking for an excellent 4K monitor with really bright colors and overall brightness for viewing content and gaming in HDR, then this is it. But if you are looking for the best response times and don’t want to tweak settings out of the box, then maybe look for something else, as this monitor is clearly aimed at MiniLED enthusiasts and people who know what they are buying and how to properly set it up for the best experience. If you want a great MiniLED thats for beginners I recommend the AOC Q27G3XMN 27" for a better entry point to gaming with a MiniLED as it's 1440p and doesn't need any tweaking out of the box for a great experience if you want to try out MiniLED without eating away $500.

I first picked up this KTC 34-inch curved ultrawide (3440x1440, 180Hz, H34S18S) for my son's gaming PC, and I liked it so much that I ended up buying one for myself too. It completely replaced my old Dell 27-inch office monitor (1080p), and the difference is night and day.

I was hesitant about going with a lesser-known brand like KTC instead of paying a premium for one of the big names, but after seeing how well this performs, I'm convinced many of those expensive monitors are using similar (or the same) panels anyway. This one delivers flagship-level visuals at a much better price.
Setup was easy—plenty of ports (HDMI, DisplayPort), full ergonomic adjustments (tilt, swivel, height, pivot), and VESA mount compatibility if needed. The only minor quirk I've noticed is that it takes a couple extra seconds to wake from sleep mode compared to my old Dell, but it's such a tiny inconvenience that it doesn't bother me at all.
My son, who's a serious gamer, spent some time dialing in the color calibration to his liking (the base settings were already great for me—no tweaks needed), and once he got it tuned, he says it looks incredible. That's the main reason I'm going with 4 stars instead of 5—out-of-the-box calibration might not satisfy everyone who's picky about color accuracy for gaming or creative work, but it's easily fixable with a little effort.

4 stars—excellent value and performance!

Analyze this product review:

I got this for $279 during Prime Day, so far, I'm exceptionally happy with it. I had it running in DCI-P3, there is very slight color shifting on this monitor more so than my other non-OLED monitor, the Samsung G7 Faker Edition. I’ve found that keeping the panel on native, black level at 50 and OD setting on off or dynamic and this issue is pretty much resolved. The OD settings leave a lot to be desired, the only manageable ones I've come across is dynamic and off, all of the others cause a degree of blurring or overshoot-undershoot in the image response times.
Initial Pros and Cons:
Pros:
-Everything works as intended, no issues out of the box, do dead pixels, backlight bleed, etc., looks great.
-Stand is actually fairly decent, for the price point.
-Crystal clear image, the AG used is fantastic, I have 34GS95QE, AW3225QF and Samsung G7 Faker Edition, and in many ways, I prefer the image quality of this monitor, great flexible gaming capabilities.
-Tremendous number of settings, what I've found that works the best, Brightness 38, contrast 50, preset, user, color natural, response - dynamic, professional - screen native, blue light at 25%, local dimming set to auto, this IMO, is the best you can get this monitor at settings wise.
HDMI upscales PS4 Pro and Xbox Series X to 4K 60hz and the latter also at 1440P 120hz.
-Screen uniformity, exceptional.
-Has a more natural look than OLEDs due to their constant blue light push, it's the technology, this monitor in the right settings, reminds me of a CRT, in some ways.
-Recommend setting the black equalizer to 50, anything lower introduces black crush, higher image washout, at 50, it helps in the overall response times, look and feel, had this set to zero and the image was ghosting a lot when scrolling, panning.
-M27T6 is significantly better than AOC's offering, the (Q27G40XMN) which I bought and returned from a different seller, IMO, the two shouldn't even be considered comparable. That monitor has two big issues, DP 1.2 and you can’t defeat the brightness settings when using local dimming, it locks to 100% brightness.
-Able to do full 10-bit at 180hz over DP 1.4 connection.
Cons:
-Image shifting noticeable, used to OLEDs, instant response times, it's better than most, though still noticeable.
-local dimming greatly reduces brightness, though you can easily up the brightness to offset this issue.
-DCI-P3 and BT. 2020 look great, for very specific games-apps, otherwise, your much better off with screen native, it provides a much more natural look.
-Over Drive settings introduce a lot of panel response time issues, blurring and overshooting, this monitor works better after it's been on for 15 minutes or so, it needs to warm up, literally. I’ve found off or dynamic OD settings work the best.
-HDR on Vesa IMO looks the best, in FPS type of games, though strategy games and such, AOE, CIV, etc., Game HDR looks more natural, you're able to change a lot of settings with HDR, which most monitors lock you out of, don't believe this unit is truly capable of the specs, HDR-1400 etc., though played a few games last night, IMO, they looked pretty good in HDR. NBA 2k25, Oblivion, Baldur's Gate 3 and others look tremendously good with HDR enabled, this monitor does a great job with 1152 dimming zones and creating a colorful and detailed HDR image for gaming or even media content, such as Netflix.
-Dirty screen effect when shifting your sight from side to side, nothing major, though I've noticed it more than I would prefer, there is an ever so slight grainy effect, only noticeable in certain situations.
For the price and what's offered, I can't recommend it enough!

I purchased this for use at work and I have now had it about a week and could not be happier with it.  I go through specific details below, but I have a smaller sized desk, a computer, and phone, and some normal desk items on it.  I chose the larger version as I also need to be able to place charts and write on the desk and it fit well and I still have extra room.  I have to admit I was a little nervous after reading reviews of standing desks in general and a number of  concerns about these desks, but I have to say I am 110% happy with this purchase and would purchase it again. I cannot recommend it enough.
1. STABILITY AND MATERIALS - First, the construction is absolutely solid.  I saw some reviews saying it looked cheap, but my husband and I both agree that it is a really nice material, solid and sturdy and does not appear cheap in any way. I would have not problem having this on a desk when I had clients in a room.  I also read reviews where people said it was unstable, but I have to say mine is as solid as a rock.  I adjust the height all the time, I actually lean on it a great deal when writing on charts and never has it wobbled or seemed to tip.  Now, I don't know that you can do handstands on it, but for any type of office work it appears to be absolutely solid and stable.  My computer screen doesn't shake when I am working on the desk or when I am moving it.  And again, I put a fair amount of pressure on it when I am leaning and writing charts and I change the height several times a day.
2. ADJUSTABILITY - So this is where I think this desk absolutely shines.  I am constantly working at different levels for different tasks depending on what I am doing and occasionally I still do like to sit. Even when standing, some tasks are more comfortable if the desk is a little higher and some a little lower.  I also do sit for other tasks. This desk is 100% able to handle that.  There are no "preset" heights that you have to stop at.  I can raise and lower it to exactly what works for me for a particular task, adjust it an inch or a centimeter if needed, and it stays right there.  No collapsing under pressure, no movement.  I don't adjust to it, it adjusts to me.  I really like that there are no set intervals I have to use.  Also, it is a breeze to raise and lower (absolutely no need for the automatic/electric ones)--- smooth as butter (no clunking at the bottom like I read in some reviews).  Again, I am constantly adjusting height depending on my task, so I adjust all the time and it just takes a split second and I don't have to move a single item on my desk.
3. ROOM/WORKSPACE - I have a large monitor, a few items  and my phone on the stand (I left the computer base and some items off to the side and I still have a great amount of room.  I can open a double pocket folder and write in charts.  Just perfect.. I don't feel like I have lost any space on my desk.
4. KEYBOARD SHELF - So yes, the keyboard shelf doesn't move in an out (that would be nice), but after a day I no longer find that to be an issue.  The shelf is large enough that I can move the keyboard here or there as I need it so that I am comfortable at any level.  When the desk is fully down I am still 100% comfortable typing on the keyboard on the shelf without any issue.  The first day or so it took me adjusting the desk placement on my whole desk to find where I wanted to stand, where my hands automatically placed on the shelf vs. where my screen was and where the mouse was-- but after slt adjustments during the day (moving the keyboard to one side of the shelf and the desk a few inches to the left or right), I got it just right and now it feels perfectly natural to walk up to my desk at any height and start working.  I would encourage you to play with the location of your screen and the whole desk on your main desk so that you find the sweet spot for everything and that will help greatly.  Don't just put everything in the very center and assume it will feel right for you.  The keyboard shelf does have a knob so you can adjust the angle of the shelf if you want, but I have to admit mine is just flat and it works well for me, so I can't comment much about the angle options.
OVERALL I am completely thrilled with this desk and would recommend it without hesitation.  I love it!!!

I saw a video about this monitor being available for $70 on black Friday pricing. By the time I got around to buying it, it was $85. I bought two of them, and I'm very happy, but there's some caveats I think you should know.
This monitor does exactly what it says on the tin... and no more. It has one HDMI and one VGA input (why?) and that's it. It takes in audio via HDMI and has a headphone out jack, and even has volume control on the control nub, but no speakers. It takes 19v power from a barrel jack, but you can swap that for a 20v supply from a USB-C brick with the right adapter (you want the 6.0x4.4mm barrel).
The HDR is rubbish, the VRR works fine. The picture quality is plenty good but not remarkable. The settings are pretty minimal and sane out of the box, you'll tweak one or two of them and then never touch them again.
The stand is a joke. Of the two of these I bought, one of them was missing the 2 required screws to mount the display to the stand. Fortunately, it has a 100x100mm vesa mount on the back, though it doesn't come with screws for that either. I put mine on monitor arms, and threw out the stands.
Basically, if you need a 24" 1080p 120Hz display, and nothing else, of good quality, for as cheap as possible, this is it. For everything else, you'll have to pay more.

There’s a bit of possible Sony hate going on in some reviews, like others I got burned on a pair of WF-10004XM refurbished and one of the batteries started failing after a year. Wasn’t worth the cost of repair. Have others from QCY and Soundcore that were surprisingly good for less cost. Also had trouble with refurbished headphones WH-1000XM4, luckily had added insurance. Cut to buying a new pair that have been flawless.
Got the Sony WF-C700N a couple months ago to scratch my earbud itch. Very good for the price. If you’re not ready to throw down $300 for the XM5 they’re a great alternative. Not quite as musical, but no gripes anyway. You can get picky about the throwback buttons but oh well.
One comment before I get more specific on the XM5. I fully agree with another review that calls out Sony for how complicated their Sony Connect app has become. It could be simplified for people who don’t want to get into the tech so much.
Now, how do they sound? I’m impressed and I’m not using them to their full potential. Using with iPhone so Bluetooth SBC codec is the most basic and lowest quality solution (after digging into the codec question a bit more it does appear that the iPhone has the AAC codec also). However, with the help of Sony’s equalizer and DSEE function I’m very happy with the sound. I almost don’t want to try them with a better codec and then have to go back. (Still applies with AAC, DSE does improve sound)
I need treble boost for my old ears and having played bass no surprise I like a lot of bass. These don’t disappoint. I did an A-B comparison with the XM4 headphones and they didn’t have quite the low end but good and punchy with good definition between bass and drums.both can become nice and “growly” on the low end.
Noise cancellation is very good, not as good as the headphones but after only a couple days I have been quite satisfied so far.
Comfort level is better than the XM4 buds, but I’m so pissed I wasted the money now I don’t want to dig them out to compare audio! I think Sony really improved the fit and design to be lighter, more comfortable, and have impressive sound. Let’s just hope they found a better battery.
Used overnight and had battery left in the morning but playing audiobook on timer so i couldn’t say how long continuous playback.
I’ll update after I’ve had them longer.
(Update) battery life seems to be very similar to the XM4. Sometimes I have battery left in the morning sometimes it comes up short.
Another follow up, comes with 4 sets of tips but apparently I have very large ear canals as I’m unable to get a complete seal with the included buds. The large felt good at first but when I used the connect app to check for airtight seals I could not get them to seal. Fortunately I have many tips I’ve saved over the years and by mixing, matching, and testing I have a couple that seal. I even tried ordering extra large tips from a couple vendors and they didn’t work either. Nice that Sony is including extra small but what about us with extra large needs! I do have a possible solution on the way, find a video on YouTube that shows how to use Sugro glue rolled up and inserted in the mushroom part of the tip. Press in the ear to get a fit and then allow to cure over night. Hoping it works, I have a few tips I’d like to try this on. Was even investigating custom molded tips but for $150 plus I’ll try the Sugro hack…
8/5/23 tried the Sugro hack yesterday. Still have to work to get an airtight fit but it definitely helped.
My opinion on the sound has not diminished. Excellent with what I listen too. A lot of classic rock but also new material from Elle King and others. Listening to Lourdes “Royals” a very deep bass which presents low, solid, and clear. You can easily distinguish the bass and drums. The low rumbling bass of Pink Floyd “Welcome to the Machine” couldn’t be much better in any buds. Almost like I could feel it.
I’m now using the WF-C700n as my workout and dog walking buds. Sound signature is very similar but the bass is not quite as good. One thing they are lacking is the airtight fit check in the app. I had to use other tips and the Sugro mold hack to get a good consistent fit in both. The included tips are worthless to me and my big ears.
I see a lot of criticism of the noise cancellation for the XM5. I have no way to measure so it’s pretty subjective but I’m not disappointed. At least as good as the XM4. But with any ANC earbuds the airtight seal is critical.
If you’re not ready to throw down $300 the WF-C700n are a very good alternative, but are not touch controlled, a single button on each side. Not quite as good on the low end but not disappointing either. In direct comparison you can hear the difference.
I still think these are 5 star worthy. I’d take off half a star because of the somewhat complex app but if you like to tinker with the sound and features, give it back. People who are not “technical minded” may find it intimidating. I find it useful but jammed with some features I wouldn’t normally use, like automatically changing settings depending on location as an example. Some might find it useful but not me. The equalizer and clear bass functions are excellent. DSEE function makes a noticeable difference in sound quality. Happier with these than I was with the XM4. Just hope the batteries last, I would hope Sony changed from the $70 replacement cost batteries (not including labor) used in the XM4 as apparently so many people had problems with them dying out after a few months.
9/22/23
Used these today instead of the WF-C700n for my indoor cycling and to walk the dog. Usually I do those activities with the cheaper buds as for $300 I want to take every precaution to protect them. So…more feedback on the ANC. Definitely a difference on the bike with 2 pretty loud blower fans on. The WF-C700n does a very good job in the same situation but I could definitely tell a difference. Could hardly hear the fans at all and the WF-1000XM5 does have the superior sound performance. Note these blowers are loud enough that if I have my Apple Watch to close to them I get the over 90db warning. They’re not 90db from the bike but they are loud. These cancelled almost all the noise. With volume on my music I don’t hear the fans at all.

I bought these because I had a gift card to spend, and in hopes that I could completely separate from my Airpod Pro’s (1rst gen). I wanted to get rid of my Airpod pro’s because I have become so completely fed up with popping them in my ears and having only one earbud connect. That happens about 25% of the time I use them, and of course it’s always right when I’m in a hurry and need them now. I have to reset them every time it happens and frankly I’m fed up with it – unacceptable reliability.
So, it’s only been a little more than a week but I haven’t had this happen once. Nor has it ever happened on any of my other true wireless earbuds (Soundcore Liberty 4 NC’s and some cheap no-name sports hook-style earbuds). The Sony’s have had stellar reviews, but my one reservation was that I’m in a full Apple ecosphere, and I had read that if you’re in the Apple ecosphere, you’ll want the Airpod Pro series II. Using anything else would mean missing out on that typical Apple integration – things work great together. Well, I’ve never tried the Airpod Pro II’s, but I couldn’t get myself to reward Apple by ordering another pair of headphones from them after my dissatisfaction with the AirPod Pro I’s.
So, how are the Sony’s? Absolutely fantastic and boy, am I glad I went with them! First of all, in terms of integration/functionality with my Apple world, best I can tell so far its flawless. Transitions between my iPhone 15 and iPad Pro are just as smooth as my AirPods were. I can send/receive calls just as easily, and the Sony has one feature I don’t think AirPods have – you can just nod your head to answer calls! I also find the touch sensor vastly superior to Apple’s squeeze surface (or whatever it’s called). Much more intuitive to me, and it works every time on the first try.
Another big advantage the Sony’s have over the Airpod Pro I’s is battery life. One reason I picked the Sony’s was better sleep. My wife makes quite a racket sleeping at night and I had read that these were great for sleeping. My Airpod Pro’s were also quite good at that, but they wouldn’t last through the night – only about 4.5 hours (w/NC on). Not sure how long the Sony can last, but I’ve gone over 8 hours (w/NC on) – and they still had some battery left! As for the noise cancelling, I’d say it’s slightly disappointing. I also own the over-ear WH-1000XM5’s, and they have AWESOME noise cancelling! I’d say the WF-1000XM5’s are nowhere near that level – I’d say they are about the same as my Airpod Pro I’s. Good enough to attenuate my wife’s snoring (at least enough that I can sleep), but not completely block it (so I hear nothing at all) as on the WH-1000XM5’s. But of course, the WH-1000MX5’s are way too big to sleep with (full size over-ear headphones). Another minor disappointment is no “find my earbud” functionality, which makes me a little paranoid about losing them, but hopefully not a big deal.
Saving the best for last is the sound quality. I bought the big-brother WH-1000XM5’s a year ago and was quite surprised at their sound quality. Same thing here – these sound fantastic! I’m a fairly serious audiophile and have quite a collection of high-end headphones, including one pair of earbuds that are more than triple the cost of these Sony’s (JH Audio J13 v2’s). And all the electronics to go with it (DAP’s, DAC’s, amps, cables, etc.). They took a while to break in properly (maybe 30-50 hours) but they are really wonderful. They are among the most natural sounding earbuds I’ve heard and I’m a bit stumped how that could be possible since it uses crappy Bluetooth. My high-end headphones are fed almost exclusively high-rez files. Bluetooth AAC (can’t use LDAC on an iPhone) is the best I can run, which of course are only a small fraction the bitrate resolution of true high-rez files. But somehow these sound absolutely wonderful – just a natural “rightness” that’s hard to describe. BY FAR the best bass I’ve ever heard from an earbud. They have a confidence, an “assertiveness” (yes, that’s a new audio metaphor) – not aggressiveness - that I just love. I’m not saying that they are flat-out better than my high-end earbuds (my Shure M535’s are my favorite), but I will say they are at least in the same ballpark. I can pop these in and really enjoy listening for hours – and not feel like I’m missing out in not using my much more expensive earbuds. Very high compliment indeed! So, great job Sony! BTW, I read that Sony bought Audeze (high-end true audiophile headphone brand), which means I can’t wait to see what they come out with in the future – if these are as good as they are, I can’t wait to find out what the XM6’s or XM7’s will sound like!
Update 4/16/24: Just wanted to mention one more remarkable thing about these. I am an avid cyclist and I’ve been on a long search to find the best earbuds for cycling - which for me, is mostly about reducing WIND NOISE. That is by far my biggest goal for cycling headphones. These are downright spooky in their ability to hugely reduce wind noise - BY FAR the most effective I’ve ever tried, and I’ve tried quite a few (AirPod Pro’s, Soundcore Liberty 4 NC, etc…). So now I face an interesting dilemma - do i dare use a $300 pair of earbuds for cycling? The problem with using them for cycling is that cycling is of course brutal on earbuds (constant sweat). So I’ll have to decide if I dare to do that long term, but I can say that these are by far the best headphones I have ever used in terms of wind blocking. So these really are amazing - fantastic sound, powerful noise cancelling, long battery life and the best wind noise blocking I’ve ever heard…

Very nice monitor, performance is excellent for a VA screen and the build quality is very good. I've been using Dell monitors for years but recently switched to Samsung as they have good monitors for a decent price. However this Dell is much better for daily use, the screen is much more clear and there's more options for customization, text has deeper contrast and the colors can be more saturated if needed. It takes some time to figure out all the settings and get everything set just right but in the end it's a much more enjoyable viewing experience.
The higher refresh rate is definitely noticeable on higher framerate games, there's less tearing when shifting your view or when rotating around a busy environment, and the transitions are smooth. I'm not able to enable HDR with my system but that's ok as I've never liked it on any of my other monitors, too dim and the colors seem washed out compared to non-HDR. This monitor is very bright, which is exactly what I wanted, I'm running this at 75% brightness which is easy on the eyes and matches my other 32in monitor which is maxed out. I really like having the ability to make the screen brighter than needed, which is not typically the case with most monitors. If I set the brightness to 100 it keeps the image quality and doesn't look washed out.
I notice a slight dimming around the borders of the screen but it's not distracting and goes away when looking directly at the edge. Due to the size of the screen it's not easy to look directly at all edges so some dimming is expected. At extreme viewing angles the screen appears less focused. 32-inch is a very good sized monitor and works perfectly if it's closer to 2ft away, any closer and it's hard to track items moving across the screen. The screen weight is about average, much lighter than it looks. I'm using a gas spring type of support arm and there's no dropping over time, the 100x100 VESA fits perfectly and the screws are included with the monitor, which is very nice.
Overall its an excellent monitor and I will be replacing my second screen with another one of these Dell monitors.

TL;DR: Very nice big monitor, no problems.
After a week of adjusting to it, and fiddling with my desktop PC to transition from a perfectly satisfactory Acer 27" 1440 100Hz 1ms IPS monitor to this new 32" 4k 120Hz 4ms Dell, I'm very satisfied with it.
Out of the box, Dell's 'Custom Color' setting seems already well calibrated; colors are not overly saturated cartoons, skin tones are lifelike. The panel appears so bright in my non windowed, small desk lamp lit home office that I'm able to reduce Brightness setting to 35%, which helps its already deep blacks become even more impressive. Contrast set to 85%, Sharpness 70%, Dark Stabilizer to setting 1, HDR Off. The right side, back-of-monitor joystick function is highly intuitive and easy to use compared to the confusing button pushing sequence of other types of monitor interfaces. (Though I also downloaded Dell's mouse driven, desktop monitor adjustment app from their website, I've yet to need it.)
Viewing 1080 live streamed broadcast of NFL games shows no motion blur at its 120 Hz refresh rate, and the 4ms response time appears to be a non factor for my applications, since I'm not a gamer. Netflix 4k material is stunning on this Dell, and I have mixed feelings about HDR's effects; I usually leave it Off. Viewing and reading web content is comfortable, with similarly responsive mouse scrolling and sharp text/graphics to my previous 1440 monitor. I enabled 120Hz refresh rate in Windows, and had to tweak appearance settings in both Windows 11 and Chrome's browser for font and text size and page zoom to maintain similar, comfortably legible open tabs' sizing to page ratios as my old screen's smaller size.
Coming from IPS monitors, the typical off axis color alteration of this VA type panel when viewed even slightly from the side is a kind of disappointing tradeoff for its 50% better contrast ratio. Appearance becomes washed out quickly unless seated in the sweet spot directly in front of it, but I'm getting used to it. The monitor's very stable stand offers generous adjustments including height, rotation and tilt, and setting a slight panel tilt upward helps to maintain best viewing angle while seated, reminding me of how amazingly sharp and beautiful this display is. I can now comfortably watch this larger screen from 3 to 4 feet away to enjoy a more immersive view of sports and movies.
It was considerably discounted for Black Friday, and arrived in an enormous, comically oversized but lightweight plain brown box to conceal its identity. It wakes reliably fast from sleep, its power cord is just that; not another cumbersome adapter brick, and I'm quite happy with its performance thus far.

I've had the same white toaster for over 20 years, and though it still works, it looks its age.  I remodeled my kitchen several years ago and all of my appliances both big and small are stainless steel.  My poor old white toaster not only looked out of place, it looked a little sad.  Some of the white color on the top of the toaster had turned from white to yellow, probably from the heat radiating out while the bread toasted over all of these years.  I've wanted to replace it for some time but never came across a toaster that I thought would due justice to the rest of my kitchen.  Until now.
When I saw this Hamilton Beach toaster on its website I knew this was the one I was waiting for all of these years.  It looked very modern and very classy. Best of all it's stainless steel.  And from what I could tell from the photos on the website it also looked well made.  I ordered it with the hope it wouldn't disappoint.  It most definitely did not.
Hamilton Beach has always made a quality product for over 100 years.  Apparently they still do.
Not only does it indeed look fabulous sitting on my counter, it works perfectly -- if you get the settings right.
When I received it, it was preset to "6" on the toaster dial.  Though I did skim the instructions before using, I decided that the preset must be the perfect setting for toast so I left it there.
I popped in the first piece of bread, pulled down the lever and pressed the 1 slice button on the front.  That button lit up very nicely making it easy to see it was working, which I thought a cute feature to have on my new toaster.
I stood there while the toaster toasted away at level 6.  I felt as delighted as a child with a new toy.  Soon the bread popped back up --- perfectly black.  I laughed at myself and replaced the burnt piece of bread with another slice.  Then I turned the dial down to five and tried again.  Still too burnt for my taste.  I tried a slice on level four and then 3, taking pictures of each level of toasting as  you can see in my picture.  I stopped at 3, because I thought it just perfect for me.
Level 6 I found out later was almost perfect for a frozen waffle.  So like any new device you decide to add to your home, it takes a little trial and error to get the results you want.
In any case, it looks so pretty and performs so well I was sorry that I hadn't found it sooner.  Naturally it's super easy to use and cleaning it is a breeze.  All you have to do is unclip the little tray in the back, one under each 2 slice section, and wipe out the crumbs.  Then the trays easily slide right back in and clip into place.
I also like the fact it has a cancel button to stop the toasting process, should the bread shift and start to burn.  With my old toaster I always had to unplug it to get it to stop toasting.
Hamilton Beach pays attention to detail so this toaster seems to be as well built as it looked on the website.  Obviously I highly recommend this product --- what's not to love?

The Aula F99 is a "96%" mechanical keyboard that comes in around the $90 price point normally, but can get as low as $60 on sale. That form factor means that it does have a numpad and arrow keys as well as home, delete and page up/down keys, but those keys are moved up in-line with the function keys and the numpad/arrow keys are squished up closer to the main keys with the arrow keys set a little further down to make space. Having a numpad was a must for me because I like to play games that often use the numpad for important functions, and I also prefer typing numbers on a numpad when the occasion arises. At this price point, this is probably one of the best options for people who want a numpad and/or arrow keys but still want a keyboard that looks and sounds more like a custom keyboard you see in YouTube shorts of people doing sound tests.
It has linear switches meaning there's no "bump" or clickiness to them, I'm not 100% sure what exact switches they are because there is some conflicting information online. I think mine has "Star Vector" switches? Regardless, the switches are quite light on force and very quiet, which brings us to the sound. This keyboard sounds great for the price. It's a little on the clacky side, but the switches have no scratchiness to them and are obviously pre-lubed, and there appears to be some kind of sound-deadening material inside the case as there is none of that hollow pinginess you get from something like a cheap Logitech mechanical. Overall it is a massive improvement from the Logitech keyboard I had previously to this one.
The case is plastic but seems to be fairly high quality. The keyboard is surprisingly heavy which is very confidence inspiring and gives you a very stable feeling typing experience. It also has RGB lighting on all of the keys but the keycaps are not shine-through meaning the lettering doesn't light up. If that's a big deal to you, I'm sure you could swap them out for something else later as it does come with a keycap and switch puller, which also means you can change the switches if you want. It also has 3 different connection modes: "Wired" which uses a USB-C port on the board for connection (and it does come with a USB-C to A cable in the box), "2.4 GHz" which uses a little wireless dongle that sits in a little slot on the top edge of the board when not in use, and it's also able to connect via bluetooth. I haven't tested the battery life as I use this keyboard at my desktop computer with the wired connection, but having the different modes and a physical switch to change between them means you could have this board connected to multiple different devices and switch between them whenver you want which is cool and useful if you need that.
I'm fairly new to the world of mechanical keyboards, this is only the second one I've ever owned, the first being a Logitech board that didn't sound or feel nearly as good as this one. As I type this review out on this very keyboard, I find myself liking the sound and feeling more and more. I'm sure there are things about it that someone with more knowledge and experience could pick apart and criticize, but overall I am very happy with this keyboard and would definitely recommend it to anyone who's not an expert and is looking for something better than the offerings from companies like Logitech and Razer.

Ok, so after spending a couple weeks with this board I can tell you-
A couple of things I wasn't really aware of-
1) Just how much pressure I'm used to applying at rest on keys
2) How much I relied on outside esc and ctrl keys for orientation
These keys are very sensitive compared to the old BW I've used for years. I've been accidentally entering a lot of keystrokes at rest. They are very quiet and soft stroking compared to the green switches in the older Black Widow I've retired. So if you want clicks, feedback or resistance look elsewhere. Believe it or not my main hesitation for getting this board was the outside left row of programmable keys. I was afraid that it would be in the way and get confused with my escape and control keys, which yes has been very challenging to get used to, but it's no fault of the board itself knowing what I was getting. I pulled up all those caps on that row and replaced with wider pudding caps for brighter distinction. Programed those keys to mirror their neighbors, esc ,Ctrl etc so that when an erroneous keystroke is made it should at least still be the function I was looking for, albeit orientation may be off from wasd. So anyway I'm having to look down a lot more at the keyboard and retraining my mind to orient off the *F key

I like that the case is slightly smaller because I do carry my earbuds around in a case hooked to my keys. Still waiting for my case to arrive, but they'll be taking up less space than my previous pair. One thing I noticed is that they connect MUCH faster than my Beats did. There is no lag at all, the second I take them out of the case, they pair. Beats fit more snugly and a bit more comfortably, but after swapping the rubber heads to a size up, these fit nicely. Still adjusting to how they feel in my ear, but that seems to be a familiarity issue rather than a flaw. I have not yet worn them during exercise so I can't speak to how well they stay in, but I haven't had any issues using them at my office job. Noise cancellation was not my main priority because I usually only have one bud in at work, and if I'm exercising outdoors I like to have awareness of my surroundings, but I do think the noise cancellation is better on these than on my beats. I've noticed even with only one earbud in, I've not noticed people talking to me as easily. The case charged up very quickly to a full charge and I've had one earbud in for the better part of an 8 hour shift and it's still working great. Another feature I think is SO smart is that the rubber pieces that insert into your ear also have a mesh pattern which covers the actual wire mesh filter that sits inside the earbud preventing that from falling out or, worse, into your ear. Those mesh filters on my Beats constantly fell out and have been lost for a very long time. I'm no advanced audiophile, but to me the sound quality is more or less the same as before. At the very least, there is nothing about the Beats buds that are worth roughly $100 more than these. I have not tested the microphone for phone calls, and I won't be, it's just not something I use or need. I do think that they should have come with a carrying case due to how small and sleek the case itself is. Easy to remedy with a case ordered separately, but it would have made them feel more high quality. Initial pairing was common sense but a gripe I had was that the instructions were images only, no written text, and I had to find out from a YouTube comment section that for them to pair successfully you have to remove the buds and remove a teeny tiny piece of film off the bottom of the buds. The instructions neither pictured nor mentioned anything about that and it would have saved some frustration and extra googling had that been included. If these can last as long as my Beats Studio Buds did, then I can't think of a reason to pay the premium for a name brand earbud. Very pleased!

We have a little land and a John Deere Z920M zero turn, and its loud. My neighbors all have the same mower, and all wear headsets. I now won't mow without my A40's, as the noise cancelling is even better than my 1 month old top end hearing aids (thanks VA).
The sound is not like you're sitting in a studio listening to an album on a top end everything audio, but nothing is, so when people try comparing buds to studio headsets, I just smile. The sound is crazy good for a couple of marble sized devices that connect via a rf signal. Darn amazing.
Update - I submitted a warranty claim, due to the right earbud not being active when I started this morning, but I decided to put them back into the charge case for a few minutes and it came to life. Here's to hoping this is not a new trend? Still love their sound quality, and general fitment. I have noticed that they have started to come loose when I'm bent over working in the heat. I've been tempted a couple times to buy new buds, but these are still very hard to beat.
Over the last two months I've tried several earbud, all were horrible failures. These are different. Shortly after I got them I headed from N. FL to Delta Junction AK. So 9 total hours in the air both directions. While there I spent 5+ hours a day running a chainsaw, a stump grinder, and a commercial wood chipper, all while using the noise cancellation (N/C).
I never ran out of battery life while running N/C, although once I left the first leg of my flights, I did put them back in the case, so each leg they were returned to full charge. Only once did I have one come lose from my right ear, and it did not fall out. Before I left I'd use them to run my John Deere commercial mower for the two hours it takes to mow the yard, and they were awesome at cutting out motor noise.
Wear - With the correct tips they work flawlessly. They have a fit process called Real Ear ID (or something like that). The testing will determine the best fit and seal by running those tonal sounds you're used to in hearing test booths. I was never able to get a passed or perfect fit according to the test, and I did try three sets of the foam tips (these did not work in my ears, and they did not allow the buds to charge in the case). As I said they stay in your ears.
Charging - The case is small and give you a full charge in well under an hour. There are only 3 led charge indicator lights, and I've never had less than 3 lights. The case also has the USB-C type charging port, unlike half of the other buds I tried, which still had micro USB. There are no good case covers that I found on Amazon, but I bought a soft case cover and it works ok, where I'd rather have a hard cover.
Touch control - the app allows you to change the function of single, double, triple touch, and long hold. The touch is responsive, and accurate.
Wear - Possibly a kind of repeat, as I've discussed fit, but I wanted to cover comfort. I do not get wear fatigue.
Sound and volume - The sound is easily as good as my Samsung Ear Buds Pro with much better battery life. Volume seems to be a problem with most earbuds, but not these. I'm older with hearing loss, and like to listen to my music louder than is comfortable for most. I end up around 45% of volume for regular listening, and around 70% they become too loud, but the sound is still clear and crisp.
The App - It is simple, but complete, with EQ function.
I've finally found a set that I'll keep.

I have a Love hate relationship with these. First let me say I've had a pair of Life dot 2's and A1's both also made by anker but with a slightly more active design that incorporated Rubber buttons, And Silicone Ear flares of different sizes to help hold them in. These Space A40's do not have as strong of a bass as the Soundcore life dot 2's or A1's they do have a cleaner very clear sound so If you like classical slow music or podcasts watching movies etc they're good there, and the Noise canceling is awesome. They also feature a small very compact case and they look very sleek with the black and silver. Now for the cons that keep my opinion of them for my own use on the fence after having them for long enough to use them for everything. These do not have bottons. they are touch sensitive and sometimes do not register the amount of times you touch them, so you get the wrong input meaning I wanted to change the volume and instead skipped my song, or vise versa very annoying. They also feature a completely plastic body with only silicone utilized for the tip. so They're quick to fall out of your ears if you exercise or work up any kind of sweat, and when you touch them to adjust them in your ear they usually do something you didn't want them to do because of the touch sensitive design instead of buttons lol... They also are only IPX4 rated which is only water resistant in the case of water or sweat getting on them, so if you drop them in water they're likely toast unlike the Life dot 2's which are IPX5 and The A1's which were IPX7 rated meaning fully submersible for a small period.
My overall assessment of the Space A40 earbuds is these are great for low activity users who are not intending on having a real strong bass and want clear audio with good noise canceling and a good battery life. I think for the price they're good compared to other makers but I feel like it's a shame that anker has made very similar earbuds in the past (lacking the compact case and sound canceling) that were more water resistant, stayed in your ear better and Had physical buttons for roughly $20 less and they discontinued them leaving these the most similar design which unfortunately just falls short for the people like me who like relaxing at home or on your work break listening to music, podcasts, shows etc and then later going for a jog or lifting weights because of their lack of retention in your ears and the buttonless design. I will keep using these as they're great, where they're good. but for the active lifestyle they leave you wanting more in places their previous similar models didn't.

Analyze this product review:

I was honestly considering returning this, but now I’m a bit undecided. Maybe I’ll write this review and it’ll help me decide.
For context, I’m a big watch person - especially for workouts - so I set a budget of $50 max and decided to give this one a try. It was right on the money. When it arrived, I’ll admit the packaging made me a little skeptical. Usually, presentation says a lot about the product, and this didn’t give the best first impression. AT ALL.
After opening it, the watch itself did feel a bit flimsy at first (see photos), but surprisingly, the actual build quality turned out to be better than expected. It feels fairly sturdy, which was a nice surprise.
I tested it at the gym this morning for the first timr, and it definitely held its own. The workout tracking exceeded my expectations - it offers a wide variety of activities you can easily select, which is a great feature!
The battery life is exceptional! It lasts for a very long time which is ALWAYS a plus!
I also liked that I could customize the watch face with a personal photo. However, there’s a downside: if you upload your own image instead of using one from the app’s store, you’re very limited in what data can be displayed. Instead of showing time, date, steps, calories, etc. all together, it only allows you to display one or two items. In my case, I could only show the time and date, which was disappointing.
Cons:
The app is probably the weakest part of this product. There’s a “Find My Phone” feature, but it disconnects every few minutes. You have to reopen the app to reconnect before using it again, which defeats the purpose - especially if you’re trying to locate your phone when it’s lost. Not sure how someone is supposed to find their lost phone but need their phone and watch need to be connected to the app before using this tool. Make it make sense??? You can’t lol.
It also claims to support notifications from apps like Snapchat, Facebook, and Instagram, but despite enabling everything, I haven’t received any of those. Not a single one. I only get basic notifications like calls, texts, and a few random apps.
I work in software, so I’m prettyyyy comfortable with tech. If I’m having trouble getting these features to work properly, that’s something to keep in mind if those functions are important to you. Please be aware of this if you’re searching for a watch solely for this reasoning.
Another downside is that the wristbands aren’t interchangeable - there’s no easy way to swap them out, which is limiting. Which really sucks.
Overall, for $50, it’s decent. But honestly, for an extra $20–$30, you could probably find something much better without all the disconnection issues this one constantly gives you.
I’ll give it a few more days before deciding whether to keep it or return it. More than likely I’ll be returning to get something more reliable but I’m writing this review for those who wants to stay in a reasonable price range, while giving them the honest review they deserve before spending their hard earned money.
Hope this helps!!
EDIT 5/24/26: I ended up keeping the watch. The more I used it, the more features I was discovering both in-watch, and in-app. However, I’m still keeping it as 3 stars because of the Cons I’ve listed still being an issue. I’d say give it a try yourselves and see how you like it. You can read all the reviews but it’ll affect everyone differently.

the activity tracking has been nice, i’ve done 4/5 workouts while wearing the watch and i love the way it tracks it. it has tons of different workout styles such as freestyle, outdoor/indoor walk/run, swimming, etc. and the app also has workout videos/training you can use if you’re new to it. while you’re working out it displays your HR, how long you’ve been training, calories burned, and aerobic training effect (no clue what that means) and if you’re doing a walk/run it tells you how far you’ve gone. when you’re done it tells you how long you’ve should take to recover as well. it keeps a log of all your previous workouts so you can look back on them.
i have tried to use the AI voice assist a few times but can barely hear it when it talks back. i’ve tried to turn the volume up but can’t seem to figure it out. this ain’t a function i bought the watch for tho so i don’t really care.
the display is really good, you can change the brightness depending on if you’re outside or not which makes it really easy to see. you can make it to where it turns on when you lift your wrist or to where you have to push the button to turn it on. i will say i usually have it to where it automatically turns on but somehow this feature keeps getting randomly turned off and i have to constantly turn it back on.
the battery life i think is pretty good ? i usually put it on the charger when i shower for about 15-20 mins everyday but it hasn’t gotten below 70% so i think that’s pretty good for a full 24hr period of it being used.
the app tells you a lot more info too. it tracks your sleep and tells you how long you’ve spent in REM, light, and deep sleep. it also tells you the quality of your sleep. it tells you you’re body’s energy level, your heart rate variability, your stress levels, spo2, respiratory rate, heart rate, and the ambient sound around you. you can also connect a BP cuff and scale to the app to track those and blood sugar for diabetics. overall it has TONS of info about your body on the app and watch.
10/10 recommend !

This will be the only review needed to know this is the Smart Watch to purchase!!
I have at this point probably purchased and returned more than 50 smart watches because I wanted notifications to have an audible tone and not just vibrate. With Bluetooth 5.2 it was an automatic with most of the accompanying apps you had to partner the watch with but when 5.3 came out, it became vibrate only on all apps with the exception of ONE…VeryFit. Additionally, VeryFit is the ONLY one which will register notifications from LITERALLY EVERY SINGLE APP you have which sends banner notifications to your phone, not just the 10-15 options typically seen in the other apps like Gloryfit, DaFit, FitCloudPro, HBand, etc.
In order to receive these Push Notifications on an iPhone, which is what I have, you need to go into Settings, Bluetooth, touch the “i” in the circle and check off “Show Message Notifications” and “Share System Notifications”. You must then go to the App List, find VeryFit, make sure Background App Refresh is checked and Notifications are mirroring the ones I’ve captured in my images.
The other important piece of info is the watch volume is set low when it first arrives. Make a phone call from the watch and touch the speaker icon key to allow for raising the volume.
In the VeryFit app itself, go to Device, click Notifications, be patient and wait a few seconds and the screen will expand - check off “Sync Phone Notifications” and this is where all the excitement is!
As notifications come to your phone, they will also become listed here on this page (and your watch will get the alert for them at the same time) and this is where you can Allow or Turn Off the specific notification. I have also captured this in my images for reference. As you can see, I get notifications for everything I receive on my phone. If you need more assistance, do as it says and tap the “i” in the circle on that page and you will get the detailed instructions just as I have given you now. I have also captured those in my images for you to reference as well.
This tracks sleep, stress, energy, blood oxygen level, heart rate, gives you weekly averages on all. It can track your cycle for females and ones weight. It has suggested programs to help with better sleep habits, managing weight, stress, breathing exercises etc. It has every possible physical exercise activity one could imagine. It’s waterproof, has excellent options for watch faces - many are free or you can opt to pay for some if you choose not to become a Community member and if you do, those become free then as well. You can share your progress within the community to help stay motivated if needed. You can contact customer service if you have additional questions at anytime by tapping the little blue operator floating on the page within the app as well.
There are screen protectors available, watch cases are shown available but they are too big, so don’t bother, you can change out the bands - there’s nothing you can’t do with this watch and the battery life is also fantastic, lasting me a week so far, even with all the many notifications I receive!!
Obviously, I highly recommend it!! You won’t regret the purchase! The only thing I am now in need of is finding its twin in rectangular form because I like to switch between that and round; should I find it, I will update this review with the information! I hope this review has helped!

The HDMI ports DO NOT support 4k; the HDMI Ports only support up to 1440p.  So if you want to plug in a 4K HDMI device, you will need, at minimum, an HDMI-to-DisplayPort adapter.  Probably a powered adapter. I have one to use my Apple TV 4K HDMI to DisplayPort.  DisplayPort to DisplayPort works fine.  The menu buttons are horrible, and the menus are clunky at best, but it is not much worse than most.
On the good side, the graphics quality is good.  After messing around with the settings, the color gets sort of close to my LG 4k, but the LG display is more than twice the price.  For me, this is a second monitor I will use to move things out of the way but still be able to see them.  Mainly text.  The monitor is OK and worth the money if you are just going to plug it into a DisplayPort.  In my case, I had to buy extra cables and a DisplayPort switch, so it ended up not being that great of a bargain.  The 1440 HDMI interface sucks.  That should be in the description.  It is a BIG deal.
UPDATE:  This monitor DOES support HDMI 2.0 4K @ 60Hz.  BUT you need proper cables rated at 4 K @ 60Hz or above.  I suggest getting 8K cables.
