Up until recently, I had never been much of a coffee drinker except for the occasional seasonal flavored latte drinks but I was having trouble keeping up with my very active twin toddlers. We already had a standard coffee maker but I didn't want to brew a whole pot of coffee at once and single-serve coffee makers seem to be very popular so I figured it couldn't hurt to give it a try. I had seen several different Keurigs from the basic ones to very fancy ones but wanted to purchase one that both fulfilled my needs to brew a single cup of coffee and wasn't too expensive so I opted to buy the Keurig K55 Coffee Maker in black.
When the Keurig arrived, I eagerly opened up the box to get it set up and start using it! I found it fairly simple to set up since there is a Use and Care Guide included and it's easy to follow the step-by-step instructions. I'd say the setup only takes a few minutes and then you are ready to brew your first cup of coffee. There are lights on the brewer that illuminate and walk you through the brewing process but once you are used to it, it becomes second nature and now, I don't even have to think about it, which is good in the early morning when I'm not thinking straight and need my coffee!
Brewing: To brew a cup of coffee is very simple. You'll need to turn on the brewer by pushing the power button. The power button and heating lights will illuminate and the Keurig will make some noises while it heats up. When the three cup sizes illuminate in blue, you know it's time to brew your coffee. Set your coffee mug on top of the drip tray and lift the handle for the K-cup pod holder. Place a K-cup pod in the holder and lower the handle completely until the three cup sizes are blinking. The three sizes are: small cup (5.25 ounces), small mug (7.25 ounces) and large mug (9.25 ounces). Select your size and the coffee will be ready in about a minute. If the water reservoir is low on water, the "add water" light will illuminate and the process won't continue until you've filled the reservoir. Once it's stopped dripping, you may remove your mug and enjoy your coffee! If someone else wants to brew a cup of coffee right after yours is done, all they have to do is remove your K-cup pod since they are single-use pods, add theirs and repeat the process.
Water Reservoir: The reservoir holds 48 ounces of water so you don't have to fill it up every time you want to brew a new cup of coffee, which is one of the reasons I selected this model. I make about two cups of coffee every day so I end up refilling the reservoir every few days. There are filters to use with the water but I purchase bottled water so I haven't used the filters at this point. When the reservoir needs to be filled, I remove the reservoir, take off the lid, fill it up with water, place the reservoir back in the Keurig and replace the top.
Cleaning: I feel this Keurig is fairly simple to clean. The drip tray is removable and I usually wipe it down with a damp paper towel a couple times a week and wash it in water, soapy water occasionally. I also like to wipe down the exterior since the front part of the Keurig gets splatters of coffee on it. You can also clean the pod holder, funnel, needles and water reservoir and lid. Be careful as the two needles used to puncture holes in the K-cup pods are very sharp.
Coffee Pods (the best part!): The Keurig K55 Coffee Maker uses the K-cup pods, which you can purchase nearly everywhere and there are many brands and flavors to choose from. You don't need to buy any specific brand with this coffee maker. As long as they are K-cups, they should work and I haven't come across any pods that don't work. I've been having a lot of fun purchasing different flavors and brands since I have several friends and family members who also have Keurigs so it's a lot of fun to swap coffees! I prefer flavored coffees and there are so many out there to try but my favorites are the Green Mountain flavors in Caramel Vanilla Creme and Wild Mountain Blueberry. There are K-cup pods in different price ranges and it's nice to have that option since everyone has a different budget. The nice thing with this brewer is that the flavors don't tend to blend from one cup to the next. For instance, my mom and I have brewed cups of coffee one right after the other (different flavors) and neither of us have noticed the other flavor in our respective cups. I've only brewed one cup of apple cider with this and haven't noticed the previous coffee flavor in the apple cider or the apple cider in my next cup of coffee. In this brewer, you can use all kinds of coffee flavors from flavored to medium and dark roasts to hot chocolate to apple cider. I typically choose the small mug (7.25 ounces) setting since I like the flavor. It isn't too strong or too watered-down for me but others may prefer other settings.
Programmable Auto Off Timer: You can set the brewer to turn off two hours after the last cup of coffee has brewed (included in the instructions). I just turn the Keurig on and off as I need it but it's nice to have that option.
Noise: Some people have stated that this brewer is noisy. I've found it's the noisiest when it's taking water from the reservoir and it sounds like a loud hum. It's not too loud when it's brewing the cup of coffee. I occasionally get up earlier than my husband and kids and brew a cup of coffee and no one has woken up (I'd say there is about 30 feet between the kitchen and bedrooms with the doors closed). When we have guests and they brew coffee before I wake up, I can't hear it at all.
This Keurig is made in China and mine had a packaging date of August 2016, a month before I purchased it. I've been using it for two months and haven't had any problems with it at all. It measures about 12 inches deep (from front to back), nine inches wide (side to side) and 13 1/2 inches tall. I've had several family members use it and my parents and in-laws have found it fairly simple to use after I show them how to brew the coffee since we all have different models. Ever since I started drinking coffee, I've had better success with staying more alert and awake to take care of my twins and buying this Keurig has been well-worth every penny we spent on it! I have no regrets buying it and have been having a lot of fun finding different flavors to try. As with all of my reviews and especially any appliances and electronics reviews, I will periodically update this review, add in any new information I discover and adjust my thoughts and star rating, if needed. If you, or someone you know, is interested in a Keurig, I highly recommend this one. It's a great model that is nice on your wallet and will brew a great cup of coffee as often as you'd like!
***Update 04/25/2017 - I've had this Keurig now for almost eight months and it's still working great for us! I typically brew four cups of coffee a day now to keep up with my kids and I've had no trouble with using this Keurig. When we have guests and are switching pods a lot, I never notice a strange taste at all (since we all like different flavors). I clean out the drip tray and wipe the whole machine down at least once a week to keep it looking nice. We only use bottled water in it so I've never had to use the filter. When we go away for a few days, I always wipe everything down and empty the water reservoir so it can air out and dry. I still highly recommend this Keurig if you want a good single-cup brewer that isn't incredibly expensive!

There are numerous detailed reviews of the Keurig K55 and other models on Amazon and I see no reason to repeat or refute other reviewers' opinions, so I'll limit my review to my impressions based on one week's use and experimentation with various coffees and other beverages that my wife and I have tried and enjoyed.
I don't consider myself to be a "coffee snob" but I drink a lot of coffee and insist on a good. fresh cup of coffee, properly brewed to my personal taste. For more than 20 years, I've used Saeco super automatic espresso/coffee machines such as this one:https://smile.amazon.com/Saeco-Philips-Intelia-Espresso-Machine/dp/B019771XIE/ref=sr_1_1?s=kitchen&ie=UTF8&qid=1481465394&sr=1-1&keywords=saeco+super+automatic+espresso+machine&refinements=p_89%3ASaeco ranging in cost from about $600 to $2,500 depending on the model. These super automatic machines allow you to load whole bean coffee of your choice into a hopper and at the push of a button, it grinds the beans, loads them into the brew unit, dispenses the coffee, then dumps the used grounds and is ready to brew another cup at the touch of a button. They are completely adjustable so you can brew your coffee as strong as you like, from espresso to fairly weak American-style coffee. They also have a steamer which allows you to make cappuccino and other coffee beverages. I love these machines and they make great coffee, but they have disadvantages. First, because you have to load the whole beans in the hopper, it isn't easy to change to a different coffee if other family members drink decaf, for example, or prefer lighter or darker roasts. Also, they only brew coffees, no other beverages. Lastly, they are complicated and require quite a bit of maintenance.
Enter the Keurig K55, which is their least expensive basic model but does everything I expect. I purchased it for my wife who likes to drink my lighter coffee as well as various teas, hot chocolate, cider, etc. My thought was to let her use the Keurig and to continue making my coffee in my Saeco but I've found that the Keurig makes very good coffee and suspect that my Saeco will be retired because the Keurig is so much more convenient to use and maintain and I'm completely satisfied with the coffee I'm brewing in it, perhaps not quite as "great" as that I make in my Saeco more than satisfactory, and far superior to the coffee I buy in restaurants, donut shops and convenience stores.
I won't recommend particular k-cup coffee brands because there are so many of them and everyone has different preferences. One of the main advantages to the Keurig is that there are so many choices available, with three brew strength/ water level settings, as well as a great variety of other hot beverages such as black and herbal teas, hot chocolates, ciders, and more.
You can also buy reusable k-cup holders and any ground coffee you like. This may save a little money and also allows you to choose your favorite coffee even if it isn't available in K-cups. I ordered a set of these reusable k-cups and have tried them with several ground coffees, comparing them to the prefilled k-cup versions of the same coffees. The k-cup ones are as good or better than the ones I've loaded myself using the reusable k-cups and are SO MUCH easier and more convenient to use. They're a little more expensive but still reasonably priced, particularly if you buy them in bulk from Amazon, Sam's Club, etc., or find them on sale at your local supermarket. On average, I'm paying less around 40 cents a pod for mine. Other k-cup beverages such as teas and hot chocolate tend to be less expensive than the premium coffees I buy.
The real advantages to the Keurig are convenience, ease of use and the variety of coffees and beverages you can make with it, including iced teas and other iced beverages. My wife and I can share a single machine and make our own preferred beverages quickly and easily. After she makes a flavored beverage, I simply run a shot of hot water through the machine to remove any off-taste before brewing my coffee.
Although I won't recommend specific brands due to personal tastes, I will mention that I prefer well-balanced, slightly acidic medium to medium dark roasts. I don't like breakfast blends or other light roasts, nor do I like really dark roasts such as those typical of some coffee shops such as Starbucks, although I have tried some of the dark roasts from Starbucks k-cups and others and they are fine, just not to my taste. I usually use the medium water level (7.25 oz) setting. Depending on the coffee I'm using, this usually gives me a rich, well-balanced, fairly strong cup of coffee. For some lighter roast coffees I prefer the low (5.25 oz) setting. My wife doesn't like strong coffee and usually uses the high (7.25 oz) setting. Teas, ciders and hot chocolate usually taste better with the high water level setting.
If you are considering giving the Keurig a try, I recommend that you consider buying one of the many sampler k-cup packs available on Amazon. Some are coffee only and others include assorted flavored coffee, cappuccino, tea, hot chocolate, cider, etc. The one I bought is this one: https://smile.amazon.com/gp/product/B00KSIE39I/ref=oh_aui_detailpage_o07_s00?ie=UTF8&psc=1 . It was a good choice and my wife and I quickly discovered our favorites. We've also bought a few others to try (on sale) at my local supermarket. All were good, even though some weren't to my personal taste. Once you decide on your favorites and the brew strength you prefer, you're all set to make good, fresh coffee and other k-cup beverages easily and conveniently.
I mentioned at the beginning of my review that I'm not a "coffee snob" but I do insist on good fresh coffee, brewed to my personal taste. The Keurig accomplishes this. I realize that many people ARE purists (coffee snobs, in my parlance). If so, you probably won't like the Keurig but for 95% of all coffee drinkers, the Keurig is great. I'm more than willing to give up my "perfect" cup for one that's almost as good and so much easier and more convenient to brew, not to mention all of the other beverages it will make.
I can see why the Keurig has become so popular. It fully deserves the five star rating I've given it. I highly recommend it to most coffee drinkers. I'm less convinced that it's the best solution to brew tea. It's okay but I still think it's worth the effort to brew tea by steeping it (using the Keurig to dispense hot water for brewing it if you wish). However, K-cup hot tea and iced teas aren't bad and are certainly quick and easy.

In the forty years of our marriage, we have owned several well-known brands of coffee makers. However, we feel that the Keurig K55 coffee maker has proved superior to any of our previous coffee brewers.
Last year I invested in our first Keurig coffee maker, and I chose the K15 for individual servings. This worked out so well that a few months later, I bought another for my office and I loved my second Keurig as much as I loved the first one. Then last winter I decided to purchase another Keurig, only a different model that would accommodate several servings.
I bought the K55 model because it has various featured options. This includes offering the choice for different hot beverages without the extra step to refill the tank each time with water, and this is due to the larger 48 oz. water reservoir. In addition, this enables us to make a variety of hot beverages in rapid succession, within a few seconds instead of waiting for all the water to reheat.  Furthermore, the Keurig K55 offers a personal ‘custom tailored’ brew by letting us determine the strength of our coffee, and we have a choice of three. The smallest amount for a 6 oz. provides the strongest brew and the other two servings are an 8 and 10 oz.
I like strong coffee, or sometimes I like to have flavored coffee, and my sister-in-law likes the same coffee that I do. My husband prefers a milder brew, and he never drinks flavored coffee. My son drinks tea, and likes to try different varieties and my grandson loves sampling different selections of hot chocolate.
The Keurig K55 has a fast set-up, with easy to follow and systematic directions from the manual. It offers us a variety ways to make coffee, tea or just to heat water and all without any major modifications, because it just goes from one task to another.
Below are some of the general features, and all are well designed and ‘user friendly’.
CONTROL PANEL:
All the controls are on the top right of the coffee maker and I like the flat slope surface that slightly slants down toward my eye level, and therefore, I don’t need to step on my tiptoes to read the buttons.
On the panel, there are 5 press buttons and each one has an LED light to reduce ‘user error’.
Power: Green LED
Auto Off: Green LED - (this is the automatic timer and when activated will automatically power off after 2 hours).
3 Brew Size Servings – corresponding size to the serving size and each with a Blue LED
a.  Cup Size - yields 6 oz. – which will provide the strongest brew
b.  Small Mug - produces 8 oz.
c.  Large Mug – dispenses 10 oz.
Aside from the 5 press buttons to regulate the Keurig coffee maker, there are 3 other LED light indicators.
1.  Add Water – a Blue LED will light up
If there is not enough water, the coffee maker will not work, therefore I consider this indicator as a safety feature, as well as a resolution to a possible ‘user error’.
2.  Descale – will light up with a Red LED light
This is another handy feature, to indicate necessary cleaning maintenance.
3. Heating – while the water is heating, a red LED powers on, and then powers off when the water is hot and ready for a brew.
WATER RESERVOIR:
Included with the Keurig K55 is a Charcoal Water filter Cartridge Kit with 2 charcoal filters. This will eliminate the unwanted chemical taste that is in some water systems, and good tasting water is essential for a delicious cup of coffee. The recommended life span for each charcoal filter is approximately 2 months or 60 ‘full-tank’ refills. There are several selections for Replacement Charcoal Filter-Pods available on Amazon.com.
The water reservoir attached to the left side is easy to remove with a slight lift up and outward motion. It fits inside a base and the tank is easy to remove and replace without any struggle. Alternatively, remove the reservoir tank cover, and pour water in from a bottle or a container.
DRIP TRAY:
This is much more than ‘just a drip tray’, under the cover is a 1” deep receptacle that will accommodate 8 oz. of a liquid spillover. Therefore, if the user makes an error and pushes the wrong brew amount for a smaller cup, this will save the kitchen counters and the floor from a major flood.
In addition, this coffee maker will accommodate my 7 ¼” coffee thermos by sliding the drip tray out from bottom base, and I can have my thermos filled when placed on the bottom flat tray base.
THE KEURIG K55 ACCOMMODATES REUSABLE COFFEE FILTERS:
My favorite coffee is from fresh beans that I grind myself, and therefore it’s important to me that a coffee maker will accommodate a reusable filter. The K-Cup pod holder on the K55 is very easy to remove and it literally takes less than 10 seconds. Just tap the bottom of the pod holder with a finger and the K-Cup holder slides out with ease. The reusable K-cup filter then slides in place within the groove, and works with perfection for a delicious cup of fresh ground beans, or any ground coffee.
The reusable coffer pod filter that I use is the Keurig My K-Cup Reusable Coffee Filter (Single) – and this is compatible with the Keurig K55 model.
I purchased this from Amazon last spring, and in addition, I use this same filter with my Keurig K15.
https://www.amazon.com/Keurig-5048-Reusable-Coffee-Filter/dp/B000DLB2FI/ref=sr_1_1?ie=UTF8&qid=1486296530&sr=8-1&keywords=Keurig+My+K-Cup+Reusable+Coffee+Filter+%28Single%29
In conclusion, the Keurig K55 is a well thought-out designed coffee maker, with user-friendly features. This machine comes with a ‘Charcoal Water Filter Cartridge Kit and 2 charcoal pod filters, which guarantees excellent coffee, even though we have ‘hard water’ (which tastes awful) in our water system. In addition, I love that Keurig does NOT use a breakable glass carafe, which was the thing that broke most often with our previous coffee makers.

I love espresso, but I love drip coffee too. In fact, I was an early adopter of Keurig and I've had both the residential and commercial brewers. The truth is I kind of got away from Keurig for awhile because I went on my espresso journey. Well, I'm back and I decided to get a new Keurig. First, I bought the Keurig K-Express because it was slim and cheap. It was good, rather minimalist and I liked that, but after awhile I realized I would like a smaller 6 oz cup. I found the 8 oz (the smallest size of the K-Express) too weak.
I decided to upgrade and I was deciding between the K-Elite and the newer K-Supreme. The reason I was considering the the K-Elite because of it's tried and true design, and it has even more brew size settings, and larger water tank. It also gives you strength and temperature control, something the K-Supreme Gen 1 doesn't. In the end I settled on the K-Supreme and bought it because it was a better deal and it has the multi-stream tech.
I got my K-Supreme and made a cup. Loved it right away, but then I was browsing around and was a little disappointed when I realized I didn't buy the top of the line residential model. That was my intention. There's a K-Supreme Plus! That's the machine I should have bought, although, it wasn't on sale. The K-Supreme Plus has all of the features of the regular Supreme, but also has all of the extra features of the former top machine, the K-Elite (Temp controls, Strength controls, Individual Profiles, Larger water tank, etc).
As far as this K-Supreme machine, the only concerns I have is is super light in weight, and if you read the negative reviews, doesn't have a stellar reliability record. A lot of people complaining about clogged needles. It doesn't feel like substantial machine that's built for the long haul, super plasticky. I can understand why people feel that Keurig quality is slipping in the new machines compared to earlier models.
The main issue I have now is I'll always be feeling like I'm missing out, I don't have the best Keurig. The extra features of the Supreme Plus are worth it in my opinion. That said, if you don't care about all of the extra features I mentioned, the K-Supreme Gen 1 will be fine. (There is a Gen 2 K-Supreme that corrects a lot of what's wrong with Gen 1, and that's why Keurig is heavily discounting it, to clear them out.)
The bottom line, it's an upgrade over my K-Express, for sure, but I wish I would have bought the fancier K-Supreme Plus. That's just me.

Perfect for individuals or couples who don't drink enough coffee to make a full pot and waste the rest. My wife and I typically only drink about 3 cups each morning. We used to brew coffee by the pot, but even limiting the brew to four cups, we still ended up wasting a cup.
Our previous Keurig K-Supreme stopped working, so we tried another brand that offered both K-Cup and coffee pot capabilities. We were expecting company for Christmas, and this seemed to be a good idea at the time.
The Keurig K-Supreme provides a much more robust flavor and gives a comparable amount of coffee in about half the time of the other brand. We purchased the other brand about a month before Christmas, so we could try to adapt to it. After a week, I ordered the K-Supreme and stored it until after the company left at the end of the holidays.
The K-Supreme is easy to use, fits on the coffee station counter, and under the cabinet with no problem.
If there is any fault with the K-Supreme, it is the tendency to fail after several de-scaling periods. I think the solution would be to de-scale the unit more regularly and not wait until the warning light goes off. It may be the mineral content of our water, but we do use and replace the water filter in the tank regularly. I have seen cleaning tablets offered on Amazon. I plan on giving those a try.
The only other nit to pick, and it is probably the result of using fine-ground coffee in the mesh pod that comes with the brewer. We had purchased ground coffee for use in the brewer from the other company. It works just fine and does not pass the fine grounds through the mesh, but the grounds get so tightly packed during brewing that it is difficult to clear the grounds from the mesh cup. After the ground coffee is gone, we will switch to medium grind.

I upgraded my previous Keurig coffee maker that I bought in 2013.  It was worth the upgrade.
I like how easy this machine is to use.
Easy setup:  Right out of the box there was little that needed to be done.  Just remove factory tape, plug it in and run a single water only cycle and good to go.
Taste:  I use a quality coffee.  I played with the "strong" button and that was one of the best cups of coffee I've had.
Speed: Hot water on demand.  This machine heats the water right before it hits the pod.  There is no internal reservoir the water is first pumped into to heat first.  This means the speed of use is much faster.  My previous unit had this and it took a bit longer to get that first cup.  Because there is no internal reservoir there is less places for scaling to take place.  Using filtered water also reduces this buildup.
Extraction: This unit is cooler than some other units and extracts at 192 with a final cup temp of about 165.  This is less than coffee enthusiasts recommend.  I taste no difference as my coffee still had a rich and bold flavor.  For someone who enjoys coffee without all the fine tuning this works great.
Ascetically pleasing:  I love how small this unit is and how it looks on the counter.  It doesn't have a LCD readout with the time or a way to auto set for an automatic cup.  The hot water on demand eliminates this need.  Just turn it on and you have a cup in maybe a minute.  Also, without an LCD display, less to break.
Clean up:  The area that the pod is inserted in is not concave as my previous unit was.  It can be easily wiped clean.  My previous unit could get a buildup of crud around the pod area.  That can't happen with this unit.
Descaling setting:  While I've not used it yet, I like that it has a descaling setting when I do clean out my machine.  My previous didn't have this and it took longer to run cycles.
Cons:  Factory taste!!  My first two cups of coffee tasted like crap.  I assumed this was because it was still getting the factory taste out of the unit.  On the 3rd attempt I used the "strong" button and wow I tasted a difference.  I'm also using zero water for my coffee.
Overall if you want a "no thrills" machine that makes coffee fast and very well then I recommend this product.

I love this air fryer. I honestly didn’t expect it to change the way I cook as much as it has, but now I only use my oven for large family meals on special occasions or for things like lasagna that simply won’t fit in the air fryer. It heats up so quickly that most meals are ready way before they would be in the oven and taste just as good. In fact, reheating pizza in it is better than any other method I’ve ever tried, and I've tried most.
It’s quiet, looks great on the counter (we have it out all the time and so many air fryers have that cheap plastic look), and the interface is very easy to use - to the point that my pre-teen son has even started cooking and reheating simple things by himself. More and more frozen foods now include air fryer instructions, which makes it even easier.
It's not a small device but the basket is a good size. It's a single compartment unit and, while I would like the ability to cook multiple items (in different compartments) at different temperatures and durations, it honestly hasn't been as big a loss as I thought it might.
A couple of minor issues: first, the basket doesn't sit level on the countertop and requires a good push to secure into the air fryer. 99% of the time this isn't an issue but when I cook hard boiled eggs (prick the fat end of the egg with a pin, cook on 270 for 15 minutes and then put the eggs straight into an ice bath!) they roll around and don't stay separated. A minor nuisance for sure.
Another note, if you're considering purchasing, is that the product photos are a little misleading. Since the instructions say not to crowd the basket, you should expect to make less food at once than the pictures suggest.
I didn't believe people who said that they replaced their oven with an air fryer but in my household this is absolutely true. It also means not heating up our living space by running the oven which is a nice ancillary benefit during the warmer months. I'm delighted with this purchase - it's far exceeded my and my wife's expectations!

I purchased air fryer oil; every thing needs a spritz before cooking,
For sandwiches we use butter or mayo, depending on what flavor we want, and usually use the Broiler setting.
The most important thing is not to be afraid of this wonderful machine…just go crazy and let your food-freak flag fly!

This machine is so amazing, I bought another one for my mom.

Update: I bought a third and plan to give it to my 87 year old neighbor and precious dear friend, who takes care of her 101 year old husband, because I know how much time she spends cooking to feed and care for him. When I gave it to her, her son took it out of the box for me, but I walked her through plugging it in and using the Power button, Pause, etc.  I had prepared a ham and cheese sandwich in advance, as well as a bowl of seasoned and cubed microwaved baking potatoes.  We put the sandwich in the machine and when it came out, it was golden and perfect!! Then we sprayed the potatoes with oil.  Halfway through cooking, she shook them. Her son uses an air fryer at home, so this gift is one the family will use and enjoy every day.
Update: Today I made soft boiled eggs.  Just crack eggs into sprayed oven safe bowl, Bake 9 or 10 minutes. Voila!!
Wow, we have re-heated pizza, and it is better than freshly delivered!!
Update:  If you enjoy coconut shrimp as much as I do, this machine air fries it from frozen in 8 minutes!  Just flip half way through.  oh my gosh!
update:  Yesterday I made toasted biscuits.  I had biscuits left over from breakfast, sliced them in half, and they air fried so golden and toasty-brown.
My husband re-heated 2 day old fried chicken for 10 minutes and raved, saying it was better than when he bought it fresh.
Update: This morning I sliced a bit of leftover chicken into a tortilla and rolled it up.  I made two like that, placed them in the air fryer and spritzed them with the spray. I really wanted to like this chair but, while there are things I do like about it, there are too many things I find fault with.
For context, I am 73 years old, am 6’3” and weigh in around 265lbs. My last chair was designed for big and tall people and it fit me to a tee. I worked from home for two years during the apocalypse and that chair was super comfortable and I could spend over 8 hours a day in it with no problems. Unfortunately the faux leather wore off so I needed a replacement. I retired a couple of years ago and now only spend a few hours a week in front of the computer so I really don’t need anything too fancy or expensive.
After researching a bunch of chairs, I settled on the Tralt Mesh Back Ergonomic Computer / Gamer Chair. I’ve never had a mesh chair before so I expected it to feel a lot different from my old all faux leather chair and it does feel a lot different but it’s what I expected.
The good:
1. Price. For $130.00, I think this is a pretty good deal.
2. Assembly. Fairly quick. It took me about 30 minutes to unbox and assemble but I took my time so you could probably do it in 15-20 minutes easy. All parts lined up correctly and all bolts screwed in without any problems.
3. Weight. This chair is at least 50% lighter than my old chair so carrying it fully assembled upstairs was easy for me.
4. Appearance. Very nice.
5. Adjustments. Raising and lowering the chair is smooth and easy. Control lever and hydraulic piston work well. Tilting mechanism is also smooth and easy.
The not so good.
1. IMO, this chair is NOT for anyone over 6’ if you are going to spend any time in it. The Amazon description says this will fit people who are 5’2” - 6’4”. Nope. The measurements shown in the description PHOTOS says 5’3” - 6’2”. Also nope. The front of the seat cushion hits my legs about half way up the thigh. It should hit closer to the knees. This makes me feel like I’m sitting on the edge of the chair. If the seat cushion was 24” in depth instead of 19-1/2” this would solve that problem. Also, if the lumbar support was positioned correctly, it might fit and feel better as well.
2. Lumbar support. As other reviewers have stated, the lumbar is too low and hits your tailbone, not the lumbar area of your back. This setup might be acceptable for someone shorter but for anyone 6’ or taller this is a problem. The lumbar is adjustable but it’s kind of a moot point in my case.
3. Arm rests. They are adjustable and slide forward but for taller people, even if fully adjusted forward, the arm rests still sit too far back and are not comfortable.
4. Stability. When I sit in the chair it doesn’t feel super solid. I don’t know how to explain it but I feel like I am going to tilt off to the side. It’s just a weird feeling. The chair doesn’t actually tip side to side but it’s just this odd feeling I get when I sit and even when rolling forward.
5. Weight capacity. The description says the chair has a weight capacity of 330lbs. This is probably true but, after using the chair for a while, I wonder about the longevity of the chair for someone heavier like me.
Look, as I said earlier, for the price this is a good deal. I only use the chair once or twice a week so decided to keep it as returning it was more of a problem than I wanted to deal with. If the seat cushion was 3-4” longer, it would fit my legs much better and I would be a lot happier.
My advise: if you are big and tall like me, pass on this chair. Spend a little more money and get something that fits you.

This is an impressively high-quality chair at a very competitive price point. While there are a few minor details that could be improved, the overall craftsmanship and thoughtful design make it a standout choice for a home office. One of the most impressive aspects was the packaging. The box was meticulously taped on all sides, preventing any dust or particles from entering; a level of care I wish was standard for all furniture companies. Inside, rather than using messy styrofoam that breaks apart and litters the floor, the company used neat bubble-style wraps for each part. This attention to detail ensured that even though the chair is heavy, every piece arrived clean and in perfect condition.
The build quality is excellent, starting with the solid metal base that gives the chair a reassuring heaviness and stability. Assembly was relatively straightforward for someone used to DIY projects, though a second person might be helpful if you aren't familiar with fixing things. The headrest is particularly noteworthy; unlike more expensive chairs I’ve owned where the headrest constantly slips, this one is very sturdy. The lumbar support is also highly effective, allowing you to adjust both the height and the support strength. The 3D armrests are another highlight, moving back and forth, twisting, and flipping up 90 degrees so you can either use them for support or move them out of the way to push the chair fully under the desk. The seat cushion is equally impressive, with 3.14-inch thick foam that feels deep and resilient, giving me confidence that it won't flatten out or lose its shape with regular use.
There are a few areas where the product could be refined. The armrests are made from a PU-padded material, which I find to be a negative as it is prone to friction damage over time; I would have preferred a simple high-quality plastic or a full mesh/cloth finish. Additionally, the assembly gloves included were far too small for an average adult. I also have a suggestion for the company regarding the extra hardware provided: since these chairs often come with spare screws or tools, it would be a fantastic and unique innovation to build a small, dedicated compartment into the frame of the chair to store these extra materials. I haven't seen this feature on other chairs, but it would be a very pragmatic way to ensure the spare parts aren't lost over the years. Despite these small points, this remains a five-star quality chair in my opinion.

It looks like someone might have tried to create a groove, but gave up.  Needless to say, I was disappointed and frustrated.
I reached out to Amazon through their chat feature.  (I should note hear that the person I dealt with was extremely kind and efficient).  After explaining the issue (and pointing out that the chair was an obvious prior return), I was offered the chance to return the item.  I didn't really want to do that; I just wanted the wheel I needed.  I was then offered a refund of $19.45 and provided a link to purchase new wheels which would cost $11.99 (before taxes and shipping).  I explained that wasn't sufficient since after repurchasing the wheels, my actual refund would be about $7.00!  I was then sent a new link for wheels that cost $7.99; offered a refund of $25.94; and told I could come back to request a refund for the wheels I after they were delivered.  I decided to go with that option instead.
I won't get the new wheels until tomorrow, but I went ahead and assembled the rest of the chair.  There were no other problems with the assembly.  I did it solo, so it took me about 45 minutes and it was pretty easy.
I really like the chair itself.  It looks nice and works well.  I like the ability to recline a little and to flip the armrests up.  The seat is nice and wide and I appreciate having a headrest.
I'm still annoyed that I was sent a repackaged returned item, but I appreciate the customer service i received from Amazon to resolve the issue.

The coffee maker is compact and looks nice on my counter. The instruction manual has straightforward step by step instructions for first time use and for normal coffee brewing. It can be programmed to go on automatically at a specified time which is convenient for people who work or are in a hurry in the morning. We tried this function and it was easy to do, however, since we are retired we like to prepare the coffee the night before but then press the on/off button when we get up in the morning. The coffee maker has a pause and serve function so you can grab a cup of coffee before the brewing stops. It also has an automatic shut off that turns the coffee maker off two hours after it was turned on. I find this feature to be very important because I often forget to turn it off. There are two other features on this coffee pot that I really like. First, it has a button to make the coffee a little stronger. You just press the “strength” button and a little coffee bean symbol shows up under the time. This slows down the drip and gives the coffee a bolder flavor without making it bitter or too strong. The second thing that I really like is that this machine makes HOT coffee which is the way I like it.

I had a Instant Vortex Plus 6-Quart Air Fryer which was a very good unit, but when I noticed the release of the Cosori Iconic Stainless Steel 6.5 Qt Air Fryer which has a PFAS-Free Ceramic Coating, and a Maximum temperature setting of450°F, as opposed to the Instant Vortex Plus only having a maximum temperature setting of 400°F, I decided to give the Cosori a try.  I am extremely glad I did.  The Cosori Iconic has performed flawlessly.  I am able to achieve much better crispy crust results on chicken and it seems to have more uniform results on all the food in the basket than the Instant Vortex unit.  Other things I like about the Cosori Iconic is the lack of the forced preheat that the Instant Vortex had.  On the Instant Vortex unit this preheat time was not timed so you could not just place things in the unit and let it go.  The Cosori Iconic starts timing immediately so you can set a couple of extra minutes if you want to preheat then remove the basket when these expire and the unit stops timing.  You can insert the food and replace the basket and timing starts covering the recipe time you wanted.  Another interesting feature is the shake button.  If you do the preheat thing, then hit the shake button when you put the basket back in, it calculates shake time based on the time the unit was displaying when you inserted the basket so your shake timer activates at the correct time for the recipe not on the time with the added preheat.  Reliability appears to be excellent based on the warranty period so even though my time with the Iconic has been limited this and the apparent quality of the unit would seemingly indicate excellent long term reliability.  From a safety perspective, the Cosori Iconic stays cool enough to touch on all surfaces with the exception of the area immediately surrounding the vent on the rear of the unit.  The vent directs output upward which is a plus as it directs the output up and away from any wall to the units rear which will reduce suspended grease particles and heat from blowing directly onto anything to the units rear.  The unit is also fairly quite so as to not be an intrusion if you have a kitchen adjoining your living room where family members may be watching TV, so cranking up the TV volume to compensate for kitchen noise will not be required.
Well, that was kind of rambling, but bottom line, I am extremely pleased with the Cosori Iconic air fryer, and have greatly enjoyed cooking with it.  Price-wise it is a more expensive option, but I feel it is worth every penny and will be a grate addition to my kitchen.

I had this watch around two weeks before I had to send it back. Do not get me wrong, I loved the watch fully, but a fatal flaw in the charging cord absolutely ruined everything.
I have been watching Nothing for several years now, and I have wanted to get into their universe of electronics for a while. So when a great sale came up for the CMF Watch 3 Pro and I had the money, I bought it. Shipping was quick. The box is a bit simple and straightforward.
Set up was quick and straight forward after downloading the app and signing in. If you are not already signed up on the Nothing.tech site, you will need to make an account. I put the band on the watch, toggled on and off some of the notifications, set a watch face, and I went about my day. The functions seem to be pretty good and straight forward.
I wanted this watch for many of it's core features; sleep tracking, step counter, BPM, stress levels, etc. I wasn't really concerned about calling out or answering calls on this watch, so I can't comment to that. I could read notifications from apps I allowed it to pair with. It does have some quick responses, but I did not see an option to talk-to-text like some watches have. I would clear out my messages every so often, because it does seem to have a little bit of a limit with how many it stores/receives.
I don't have a way to confirm the BPM, or the accuracy of the other main features, but I did notice something with the sleep tracker feature. I have a habit of "laying awake for a while", and I would notice that it would count some of that as sleeping/napping. Yes, it has the ability to track naps, as well, which was really cool! Everything was easy to access within the app, and I could check my stats as often or as little as I would like. It was able to help pause, forward or reverse my songs on Spotify without issues. The screen was beautiful, simple, and easy to read even out in daylight. The response was sometimes perfection, and other times there would be just a bit of a hesitation between touch/gesture. But it wasn't enough to be upset with it, you know?
The battery was phenomenal!! I could have easily gotten over a week out of it, if I wanted. I charged it when it would get down to around 40% or 20%, and it did not take long to charge the first time.
My problem comes from this; The second time I went to charge it, I noticed it was taking a bit longer than the first time. If you aren't aware. The charger cable is one of those magnetic pogo pin cables where you have to line it up just right on the back of the watch. If you so much as blink while setting it down carefully, you risk the cable popping off. Or at least with mine, it seemed to be this way. So, the second charge took a bit longer. I put the cable away safely without really looking at the cable. I ordered a second watch as a gift, and I was setting up that watch and figured I would just pull out my cable and charge it up. That is when I noticed it wasn't charging at all now. To my discovery, one of the pogo pins was stuck down.
I figured I could reach out to Nothing's Customer Support and see if I could get a replacement cable, because some of the reviews I had seen about third party cables were not super good. (See; cable melting, pogo pin area melting, melting the watch, etc.) So I emailed the Customer Support in hopes that they could help me with this issue. I was asked to take pictures. I take the pictures, and they respond back with, "We have determined to be man-made damage, we will void this product. You will have to pay for a replacement cable." If you research/Google these types of cables, read reviews even on their own Nothing Customer Support over the years, etc., you will absolutely find reports of pogo pin spring failures, pins getting stuck, susceptible to corrosion, dirt, etc. I responded that I was confused by their ability to just determine that it was "man-made damage" when this happened with no part on my doing. I take really great care of my electronics and their assigned charging cables. The cable was always stored in a safe spot. When I received the cable, I noticed that one of the pins was a little lower. I have no clue if I was sent a used watch or it was caused by potential temperature shifts/humidity between where it was stored, shipped, to my house? Either way, Customer Support sent me in circles, offering to "send me a link to a new cable", and when I would explain that I was weary of third party cables, and I was unable to find legit cords, they assured me they would send me to "verified cords".
Spoiler Alert; They would Not in fact send me "verified cord links" to purchase. Instead they asked for me to send Proof of Purchase of the watch. After I did so, they wiped their hands of me and told me to go through Amazon for a replacement, because I was still within my 30 days return window ((thankfully!!!)). When I initiated the replacement, I was only able to do the "Return" for some reason?? Amazon has changed some of their features, because I was hoping to get a replacement.
Honestly, I would have loved to have just kept the watch and get a verified legit Nothing charge cord sent, because this is a known issue with those types of cables. I really hope that going forward, Nothing CMF will find a way to use the wireless coin chargers and get away from the pogo pin type chargers. I know they are on the "cheaper side" for smart tech, but it would honestly elevate the quality, because again... I really loved the watch!!

So I am coming to this watch from an absolutely ancient Apple Watch 2. The battery on that finally bit the bullet and wouldn't charge anymore.
Not wanting to spend the 200+ dollars on a new lower end Apple Watch, I decided to take the chance on this one after reading reviews and doing some research.
First in terms of looks - This looks fantastic. The watch faces are modern and there are so many options - from more minimal to hyper functional - displaying most of the metrics you would want to see in a smart watch/fitness tracker. I got the dark grey version and it is very clean. There is minimal branding with small text displaying "CMF by Nothing" on the rim around the watch face, but it is barely noticeable. The screen is bright, and I always have mine set on adaptive brightness. I haven't had any issues seeing the screen during a bright day yet.
The biggest plus for me is battery life! This thing will not die! The biggest issue I had with the Apple Watch was the battery life. Mine would die near the end of the day, even when the battery wasn't cooked from age. I had to constantly have it on the charge at the end of the day and never used its sleep tracking because the watch would be dead in the morning if I did. This definitely does not have that problem. I've worn this watch 3 days in a row without a  charge, and even with pretty frequent use/checking it was still at 60ish percent. I usually charge it by putting it on the charger while I'm getting ready for work in the morning. It will go from 80ish percent to 95+ in the time I'm getting ready. I'm looking at the battery life right now - it is 2:30 in the afternoon and I've had the watch on me since I charged this morning around 6:30 - 95% battery life!
In terms of tracking I can't speak much to the accuracy of the workout tracking, as I haven't really approached it with a hyper analytical eye. To me it seems pretty accurate. Sleep tracking seems pretty good, maybe a few minutes off, but that is negligible for my use case. Heart rate sensor seems pretty good, and in that case I was able to actually test it against another device made just for heart rate tracking, and it was only a few beats off, so pretty good there.
In terms of using the device I've found it to be a pretty intuitive and easy to use smart watch. Swipe gestures to move around menus, it's very responsive, and the haptics are satisfying. Turning the crown control knob to scroll through menus has a very satisfying buzz at certain increments. It shows my notifications and allows for customization of what notifications come through. I have not used it to take phone calls on the watch itself - still prefer doing that on my actual phone.
The only thing I did change about the watch is swapping out the wrist band for a more elastic nylon sport band - I've found silicon bands get a bit stuffy on my wrist and I like breathability of the nylon bands more. I also added a screen protector to the watch face to help prevent scratching.
I have this watch connected to an IPhone 17 base, and have had no issues with connectivity or health tracking. You use install the Nothing app and connect the watch via bluetooth to the phone and app. My IPhone health app still shows the daily health metrics from the watch, and I haven't had any issues so far with errors or missing data.
All in all, if you are looking for a more budget friendly smart watch or fitness tracker. I would definitely recommend this. If you are looking for a very fitness oriented smart device, this might not fit the bill.

After three weeks: The watch itself is well-made and very handsome, with a metal case (mine is dark grey) and a solid feel. The OEM strap is nothing spectacular, but there are hundreds of 22 mm replacement  watch bands on Amazon to choose from if you want something more attractive. Step counting and heart rate monitoring both seem unusually accurate, as does GPS tracking of outdoor workouts (cycling in my case). Sleep monitoring is inaccurate, sometimes wildly so, even if you turn on enhanced monitoring. Unlike many competitors, engaging the "do not disturb" function at night turns off notifications but does not turn off the "raise your wrist" activation of the watch face; it has to be manually turned off and on. CMF provides dozens of attractive watch faces to choose from, including many with analog dials. Battery life is well over a week even with extensive use. The user manual isn't very helpful but multiple YouTube videos explain the Pro 3's many usual features. Customer service is also helpful. If you are looking for a reasonably priced under $100 Samsung clone with much longer battery life, and don't care much about accurate sleep tracking or an attractive app (see below), the Pro 3 could be a good choice.
Unfortunately, the app situation is far less attractive. The "Watch Pro 3" app designed for CMF smart watches is being phased out. While the online instructions say it can be used until June 2026, once you log into to the watch Pro 3 app, you are effectively forced to download a second app, the "Nothing X" app. (Perhaps after June the double app approach will no longer be necessary.)
The Nothing X app was originally designed for use with CMF's earbuds; it appears to have been recently adapted for use with the Watch Pro 3. It took me quite a while to figure out to how to get from the "My Devices" screen to the "Health" screen. In my experience with over half a dozen smartwatches and apps, I was expecting the usual icons at the bottom of the page, "Home-exercise-device-personal data" or something similar. No such luck with the Nothing X app.The health page has all the essential info but it isn't well-presented. Everything is on a monochrome page listing of steps, sleep, heart rate, blood oxygen, etc. with the same monochrome for the sub-pages. Perhaps that is all earbud users expect, but smart watches users who are experienced with "FitCloudPro Pro" or "SmartHealth" apps that feature color displays and multiple graphics may expect much more. "Nothing X" is truly "Nothing Much." I would have expected more from an innovative company like CMF.

I spent a lot of time looking at office chairs. I mean, A LOT of time.
I started with a blank canvas and wanted to see what would be better than the $50 chair I was currently sitting it.  It looks fine and has some padding, but really isn't good for sitting 4-6 hours straight in.
RESEARCH
So, do you go with the "luxury" high end chairs? What can you get for under $300?  Under $200?
- In the end I decided that I really didn't need all of the features of the top-end ergonomic chairs (synchro-tilt, 3-way adjustable arm rests, adjustable lumber support, premium headrest, premium materials) ($800-2500 chairs) - think Aeron, Steelcase, etc.
- I also decided I didn't want to spend $300-800 for one of the luxury ergonomic "wannabes" that LOOK like the high-end chairs and offer similar functionality, but with lower quality materials and build (and durability).  This range also included used high end chairs like the Steelcase 2 because shopping for them on eBay could be hit and miss (though many discussion groups I saw loved this option).
- I finally decided that for 4-6 hours a day, 3-days a week, I just wanted a chair that was comfortable on my bottom, was height-adjustable, had some tilt / tension control, and had arm rests that could flip out.  My chairs tend to do double-duty as extra dining room chairs and the foldable arm rests are critical for that.  The price range for these chairs were in the $80-180 range, and I looked at about a dozen different ones on Amazon that had decent reviews (and a lot of them).  This was my "Goldilocks" range for a chair - not too expensive, not dirt cheap, "just right".
I ended up ordering the blue fabric on black chair because I liked the look (about $125).  The white chairs with fabric seem really popular (blue/white was $180!).  After I ordered, the black leather seat chair was only $90.  This seems like a really good deal.
Anyway, the chair arrived today and here is my detailed review (so far):
PACKAGING & ASSEMBLY INSTRUCTIONS
I have included pictures of everything that came out of the 33 lb. package.  I like the fact that all of the small parts (screws, washers, caps) were packaged together with a code (A, B, C, D etc.)  The instructions referenced the parts code, so it was easy to follow the instructions to assemble the chair.  I was very meticulous, and it took me about 40 minutes by myself.  Parts of the instructions were vague about what and when the screws should be fully tightened and what they mean by "be sure the cylinder column cap has been taken off" (there was no cap as far as I could tell).  I did see a few reviews where people complained about the assembly because they had some physical limitations.  Good God, man, if it's that bad, go buy a chair at Home Depot and pay them $15 to assemble it for you!
In this day and age though, a 3-minute video helps immensely if they had done one, but I suppose you then have to do it in multiple language.  In any case, I gave this a 4 out of 5 stars.
FIT, FUNCTION, APPEARANCE and COMFORT
I would say (as other reviews have stated) this chair LOOKS really nice.  The blue adds some color to my office, and the chair has a modern look - something more than the $125 I paid for it.  The height adjustment works fine, as does the recline function and tension, though here, a short video on how to use it would have helped.  The seat and back rest are very comfortable, but there is no separate lumbar support cushion - just the curve in the lower back for that.  If you really crave lumbar support and functions, look elsewhere.  The chair also glides very smoothly compared to my old one.  But that's because dirt and dog hair haven't fouled up the wheels yet.  Alls this is good for 4 out of 5 stars.
LONG-RANGE PLANS
So, for now, I think this is a keeper unless something drastic happens with the chair in the next couple of weeks.  I think I will get black rubber or polyurethane caster wheels to protect my hardwood floors though.  Check the date of this review - 6/3/2024.  If anything major changes, I will update the review.  Otherwise, assume that the chair is still doing great.  I hope I get 5-6 good years out of it at least.  Would be ecstatic with that.

I looked through a number of Cold Brew device reviews and this one kept popping up.
An advantage of this to the others* is that it didn't require a specific, proprietary filter pad. The screen filter provided with the Oxo should last for years (I hope). You can reduce residue further with a paper filter (included). I tried it and it can clog resulting in a very slow and possibly low quantity of the filtrate (brew). I now use the advice of another reviewer and filter with the metal screen only at first, empty the coffee grinds, and re-filter the brew in the empty bowl with the paper filter installed below the metal screen. Worked perfectly. It is not a required step, the initial filtrate seemed good enough to me. BTW, you can cut paper filters from your drip coffee maker if need be.
Other than the 2nd pass for fine filtering sediment, another trick that worked well is a 2nd round of brew, also suggested from another reviewer. The recommended 5 cups of water returns approximately 3.5 cups after 24 hr brewing period (1st pass). I then added another 2 cups of water for an additional 24 hrs (2nd pass) and ended up with about 5 cups total. The 2nd pass did not seem bitter. I think that cold brew may not extract as much coffee as a hot brew, even with the extended time utilized. I'm not sure you would even consider a 2nd pass is you originally filtered with the paper filter installed.
As others have mentioned the glass beaker could be thicker and grippier. I collect the brew in the beaker but store it in an old mason jar in the fridge. The beaker feels a bit slippery from condensation if you use it from the fridge. I wrapped a couple of rubber bands around the neck as a precaution, even though I brew at room temperature and the beaker is not slippery, it is still a little awkward.
Finally, the dreaded 'leak' issue. DO NOT OVER-TIGHTEN! The O-ring is pretty flimsy and seems it can roll if pressed. It's better to under-tighter and if a leak occurs tighten a little more. If you over-tighten it will be a mess because you'll probably have to take it apart. In a review by Alloy Recon, he mentioned using a sturdier O-ring: "#142 Silicone O-Ring, 70A Durometer, Red, 2-3/8" ID, 2-9/16" OD, 3/32" Width" . Amazon was out, but did have this one:  2 3/8'' Diameter -142 Water and Steam-Resistant O-Rings (25 EA per Pack). Much sturdier O-ring!  FWIW, I'm on my 4th brew and still using the original O-ring. The suggested replacement is thicker and causes the filter screen to be looser as well. Not sure if this will let through extra sediment or not as I haven't tried the additional O-rings yet for a brew. If so, the paper filter step should clean it up.
OK, as for taste, I have not sampled different devices to compare, but there are reviews where they did. The reviews claimed this to be the most flavorful brew. Possibly as the screen does not filter as much as the filter pads would that are used in some of the other popular devices. Still a very smooth brew. Although this is the most expensive of the devices I was considering, and the additional O-rings are a good insurance policy but added to that price, the other devices required proprietary filters adding to long term cost, if they are even still available over time. I'm very happy with this purchase.
Good luck!
*The devices I was considering all produced a condensed brew of 32+ ounces that gets diluted when used. I narrowed these down to the Oxo, Toddy and Filtron Cold Brewers. This 'concentrate' was generally not the case for the devices that were simply a jar with a fitted screen tube/insert.

When I tried to install the JBL Headphones app from 'Google Play' on my Consumer Cellular Verve I couldn't find it with a search; and when trying to install from the QR code I kept getting an error message 'not compatible with your device'.  I was ready to return them until I did a search on the error and found an article explaining an alternate way to install the app through APKMirror (which to my surprise actually worked).  Having gotten past that, everything has been fairly easy and seems to work really well (except it takes some effort and usually a few tries to get them snug in my ears).  I ended up using the smallest gel caps and I suspect some people who complain about not having a large enough size might actually need the smaller size.  I set up the left bud to control volume instead of the default since I will use them only for music.  At first, I thought I was supposed to tap the top of the buds to start/stop etc. but soon realized I was supposed to tap the outside surface, and it worked fine from that point on.  One review complained about the small number of presets for the equalizer.  I think they probably didn't scroll down far enough.  In any case I just set up the custom option to match what Rock would normally be (a curve with gradually increasing base & treble at the low and high ends) and it sounds fine.  I have only been using these for a short time.  But unless there are problems I haven't encountered yet, I think these JBL Tune Buds would be much more than adequate for just about anyone (or at least those planning to use them exclusively for music as I am).
I finally got a chance to use these on an ice rink (real life situation).  I agree they are somewhat difficult to get seated in your ear.  The quick start manual has 2 pictures illustrating the suggested positioning for doing it, but I also wiggled them and pushed in for about 5-10 seconds which seemed to help.  Once I got them in, they stayed.  With my budget priced phone placed on the sidelines the blue tooth stayed connected over the entire area of the rink.  I found it very helpful to be able to pause, rewind and replay a song by tapping the ear bud (as opposed to using the phone).  For those stating they are not loud enough, check the app setting to see if you have the volume limiter enabled (and be careful if you turn it off).

Here are my comments and concerns with model YX001 only.  The instructions have a few issues imho: black letters/words printed on a dark/darker background, I literally could not read them at times and had to go to another room with a spotlight to make sure I followed directions.  A box around the words are fine, but not a colored box.  The 6 star gear shims (piece I) on the arms really needs a better way to identify instead of “placed in the direction of the instructions”.  I am not having any issues with the arms so I assume I may have gotten it right.  There aren't any instructions when to tighten all the screws that you were told to leave untightened, that could lead to an issue if when you finally get the chair finished and see step 8 saying Done and try to sit in it.  Not impossible use the included Allen wrench (great it is included!) to tighten the screws from step 4 to Done because the T-handle will not fit in the now put together space.  We have a bunch of regular Allen wrenches so I was able to complete the tightening required.  Overall assembly was not that difficult and the time to accomplish it was not longer than expected.  While the above caused some delay, the chair is still fine after 4 weeks of continuous use.
The chair itself: the lumbar support is very nice and easy to adjust.  The arms are attached to the back and the seat seemingly to give more support for them when getting in and out of the chair.  The arms lifting up and away is nice.  The seat, after a couple of weeks, seems reasonable, not too soft or too hard, the mesh back is nice, and the gas lift feels and sounds solid.  The chair would be worth 4.5 Amazon stars, except…  I’ve had a lot of office chairs (including work) over my 50+ years of sitting in front of a computer daily: cheap chairs, relatively expensive, and in between.  I have a glass floor mat and the chair does not roll freely.  There are flat spots on the wheels and it takes effort to get the chair to start to roll anywhere on my mat while sitting in it.  The description says they are soft to reduce noise and they do on my mat.  When on glass all chairs still make a noise due to the nature of the mat, so that’s not an issue.  Compared to the rest of the chair the wheels aren’t up to what I expected and I am concerned about their longevity being soft with a non-circular shape.  Perhaps on carpeted floors this might be hidden.  Lastly, be aware the description says Lifetime Warranty, however an included index card says 5 years IF you send them an email, which I did, but was ignored for a couple weeks.  Only after using Amazon to complain about them were my inquiries finally answered.  It is indeed only 5 years (NOT lifetime) which is still a decent amount of years for a chair.  I will update this if any issues appear within 5 years.

If you are thinking of exiting the Samsung Watch Eco System, this is your sign.  I have had the Instict 3 AMOLED for several weeks now.  Prior to this I have always had a Samsung watch (since 2015).  I have grown tired of constantly watching my battery and having to charge at inconvenent times.  I started looking at Garmin a bit ago, but it was always far too expensive.  Enter the Instict 3.  I puchased it not too long after its release and have found it to be outstanding...  First off, the battery lasts 18 freaking days.  As a person who loves data, and doesn't needs worthless apps and features that suck at executing on a tiny sreen, this has proven to be great.  This watch has full color, plentiful watch faces,  and features out the nose.  All the basics of course, but more accessible and accurate GPS, altimeter, and health features.  The morning health report, stress analsysis, and body battery scratch my data nerd itch, while all the typical smart watch features like text and email alerts, step counter, and fitness tracking feel like they are right on top and ready for interface.
There is one thing though, that you have to get used to.  THIS IS NOT A TOUCH SCREEN.  It isn't.  And, as someone who got used to that over the last 10 years, it took a minute.  But no matter how much you think you need it, you don't.  No matter how much you fear you won't like it or won't get used to it, you will.  In fact, back to 5 buttons and ditching the touchscreen has virtually eliminted accessing apps on accident, starting or stopping processes that I hasn't intended to, and issues with water freaking out the funcitonality.  Just take a minute to read the instructions and learn your buttons and your menus.  Then...  GIVE IT A MINUTE.  The first 24 hours are a little freaky.  The next 24 are a little annoying.  After that, you miss it from time to time, but not enough to give up what you gain.
Also, can we talk about the built in flashlight?  It sounds so hokey, and I thought it was going to be dumb.  But it is fantastic.  I use it ALL THE TIME.  Its a bright little bit of happiness.  A double press on the watch has helped me find keys, look for lost items in dark places, saved me while camping, and allows me to find things when I am trying not to wake my my wife.  It's a crazy must have that I didn't know I needed.  I could keep going.  But I have things to do.  If you are on the fence, just do it.  You won't regret it.

The Aula F99 is a "96%" mechanical keyboard that comes in around the $90 price point normally, but can get as low as $60 on sale. That form factor means that it does have a numpad and arrow keys as well as home, delete and page up/down keys, but those keys are moved up in-line with the function keys and the numpad/arrow keys are squished up closer to the main keys with the arrow keys set a little further down to make space. Having a numpad was a must for me because I like to play games that often use the numpad for important functions, and I also prefer typing numbers on a numpad when the occasion arises. At this price point, this is probably one of the best options for people who want a numpad and/or arrow keys but still want a keyboard that looks and sounds more like a custom keyboard you see in YouTube shorts of people doing sound tests.
It has linear switches meaning there's no "bump" or clickiness to them, I'm not 100% sure what exact switches they are because there is some conflicting information online. I think mine has "Star Vector" switches? Regardless, the switches are quite light on force and very quiet, which brings us to the sound. This keyboard sounds great for the price. It's a little on the clacky side, but the switches have no scratchiness to them and are obviously pre-lubed, and there appears to be some kind of sound-deadening material inside the case as there is none of that hollow pinginess you get from something like a cheap Logitech mechanical. Overall it is a massive improvement from the Logitech keyboard I had previously to this one.
The case is plastic but seems to be fairly high quality. The keyboard is surprisingly heavy which is very confidence inspiring and gives you a very stable feeling typing experience. It also has RGB lighting on all of the keys but the keycaps are not shine-through meaning the lettering doesn't light up. If that's a big deal to you, I'm sure you could swap them out for something else later as it does come with a keycap and switch puller, which also means you can change the switches if you want. It also has 3 different connection modes: "Wired" which uses a USB-C port on the board for connection (and it does come with a USB-C to A cable in the box), "2.4 GHz" which uses a little wireless dongle that sits in a little slot on the top edge of the board when not in use, and it's also able to connect via bluetooth. I haven't tested the battery life as I use this keyboard at my desktop computer with the wired connection, but having the different modes and a physical switch to change between them means you could have this board connected to multiple different devices and switch between them whenver you want which is cool and useful if you need that.
I'm fairly new to the world of mechanical keyboards, this is only the second one I've ever owned, the first being a Logitech board that didn't sound or feel nearly as good as this one. As I type this review out on this very keyboard, I find myself liking the sound and feeling more and more. I'm sure there are things about it that someone with more knowledge and experience could pick apart and criticize, but overall I am very happy with this keyboard and would definitely recommend it to anyone who's not an expert and is looking for something better than the offerings from companies like Logitech and Razer.

I LOVE, LOVE, LOVE this machine.  I didn't think I would - but I do.  I don't like owning a lot of kitchen devices as I have a small kitchen.  Additionally, I think people often buy the newest fad and then the machine doesn't get used.  I limit myself to the bare necessities in kitchen appliances.  I researched this before purchasing and figure I could return it if it didn't perform well.  This design is totally different from other air fryers.  I purchased an air fryer for a friend and while the thing worked it was bulky and I couldn't figure out how one could actually clean the thing out. I think the oil and debris must accumulate or the high temps sanitizes the machine.  I never wanted to own one until I saw how Ninja turned the traditional air fryer design upside down.  Unlike all the other air fryers, this design it so very easy to clean because the cooking element of the sits on top of the glass containers.  The bowls can be stored in the freezer or refrigerator.  Not sure if they are safe for microwave or not.  This is so more than an air fryer as it bakes, roasts, grills, etc.  Ninja doesn't advertise the machine as a low calorie way to cook but it should.  Any fats from the meat one cooks or oils added to the food ends up at the bottom of the container.  Saves lots of calories when using the grill function.  The two glass dishes are incredibly easy to clean.  One would think with the high temperatures that food would bake on and be difficult to remove.  It isn't.  This glass is somehow different and cleaning is easy and simple.  Mostly just with soapy water and a sponge unless especially dirty then scrubber side of the sponge might be needed.  Cooking has been so very easy.  Since it take relative little time to cook say chicken thighs (10 min), I can cook them and then cook some vegetables (5 min) without the meats getting cold.  Or I've been able to partially cook some baby potatoes and then stack chicken on top and finish cooking both together.  I've cooked everything from tater tots to marinated tofu and everything has turned out great.  As with everything there is a learning curve in determining how long to cook something.  When cooked correctly chicken thighs have turned out crispy on the outside while still moist.  I cook marinated tofu to be used as either a high protein snack or to be later added to a stir fry.  Believe it or not my dog absolutely loves the tofu I have been making in this Ninja.  I mean she LOVES it.  I have been using this machine several times a week which is highly unusual for my don't-really-like-to-cook cooking style.  The smaller bowl is the right size for one to two people, while the larger bowl is sized for larger portions.  With the larger bowl I was able to cook two Cornish Hens.  Their picture showing it cooking a whole chicken is wishful thinking IMO.  I don't think possible unless that is a very small chicken.  I find grilled vegetables come out great, as do baked potatoes and roasted mini potatoes.  Grilled eggplant and peppers have been very tasty.  I have attempted a sort of stir fry but since vegetables require different cooking times I found that sequencing the vegetables too time consuming. No fault of the machine as I was asking it to do something it was not designed to do.  I tried their tater tot recipe and it was pretty good.  I keep trying to create new ways to use this machine and know I have not yet explored its limits.  Sometimes if I put too much food into the smaller bowl I will get foods slightly stuck onto the heating element.  But never had any problem removing that food.  I have not tried baking cakes or anything of that sort but plan to try sometime.  This is one of the most versatile machine I have come across and the reason I would buy it again.  I've started to enjoy cooking again due to this little machine.
