Analyze this product review:

I am a Ninja fan and have quite a few of their product which I love. When I discovered the Crispi air fryer, I was hesitant to buy it since I have the dual air fryer and a couple of other Ninja appliance that also do a good job at air frying. Even so, I was intrigued by the price that is lower than most Ninja appliances, and decided to try it. I figured I could return it if I didn't like it.
As it turns out, I love it. Since I have other appliances that perform the same functions, it's not something I will be using every day. Yet the smaller size of the containers are very useful when you don't need a larger oven or other appliance for the cooking task. So, what are the pros and cons of this air fryer and would it be useful for you.
Pros:
1)  It includes two glass cooking containers, 6 cup and 4 quart, that can withstand temperatures of up to 450 degrees. I have used both containers and it not find any problems with maintaining temperature in the larger container as reported by another buyer.
2)  Lids for both containers are included for storing leftovers, but I doubt I will ever use the lids.
3)  Both containers include crisper plates that elevate food from the bottom of the containers so that air circulates around the food for even cooking.
4)  The entire unit with all of the accessories nests together, so it really doesn't take much storage space.
5)  Since the containers are smaller than an oven, they heat up much more quickly and cook food faster.
6)  Includes a recipe book with recipe ideas and charts for cooking a number of foods in both container sizes. Personally, I doubt I will use the recipes, but the cooking charts are very useful since this unit heats fast and maintains temperatures better than some other cooking options.
7)  The glass containers and crisper plates are very easy to clean. Warm soapy water and a wash rag is usually all that is needed for thorough cleaning. In addition, these items are all dishwasher safe.
8)  Super easy to use. Select a mode, recrisp, bake, air fry, or max crisp.
Cons:
1)  Since the bases cannot be separated from the glass bowls, it could be difficult to clean the underside of the bowls around and above the base. So far, I have not had anything get onto the underside of the bowls, so this hasn't been a problem. I have been cleaning the bowls by hand since they are so easy to clean. Since the bowls and bases are dishwasher safe, washing in the dishwasher would resolve this problem.
2)  Specific cooking temperatures cannot be chosen. Each mode has a temperature range that can't be changed. So far, this hasn't been a problem for me since I choose the mode by temperature range rather than by function. Bake has the lowest temperature range and is supposed to supply gentler heating. This mode works best for foods that you don't want to use the higher temperatures used for air frying, such as seafood.
Tonight, I reheated a large stuffed pepper that had been cut in half when it was partially thawed. In the past, I reheated these peppers cut in half in an oven and in a small casserole dish. As the peppers reheated, they sat in the juices released by the peppers and meat in the peppers. I used the 6 cup container, put the pepper halves on the crisper plate, and the juices were collected below the plate. I heated the peppers using the bake mode for 10 minutes to complete the thawing. After we ate our salads, I baked the peppers another 10 minutes to reheat them, and added BBQ sauce in the last 5 minutes. They came out wonderful. Some of the top of the meat was a bit crisped, and the BBQ sauce was well heated. Judging from this experience, I don't think I would recommend cooking a 4 lb. chicken in this cooker since it would be so close to the heating element, but a 3 lb. would work fine. It should be baked first on the back side and then turned to cook on the top side. When almost to 165 degrees, it should be air fried a few minutes to crisp the skin.
This appliance shines for so many uses, and would be perfect when cooking for 1-4 people depending on what is being cooked. My husband's cooking abilities are limited to the microwave and the toaster, and even he could use this appliance without feeling challenged.
UPDATE 12/05/24:
Tonight, I made a couple of lemon pepper chicken thighs for dinner. Since the thighs were small, I decided to use the small bowl of the Crispi to air fry them, and used a wireless probe to monitor the internal temperature of the thighs. I set the done temperature on the probe app to 165 degrees, used the air fry mode on the Crispi and set the time to 15 minutes since I wasn't sure how long it would take to cook the thighs. I started the cooking with the skin side down and turned the thighs when the internal temperature was at 100 degrees to brown and crisp the skin.
It took 13 minutes to fully cook the thighs. They were well browned and very moist. I will definitely be using the Crispi in the future for cooking foods that don't require the space of a larger oven.
I will update this review if my opinion changes. At this time, I would recommend this air fryer if you feel it would be useful for you.
I hope this review was helpful for you.

Another note, if you're considering purchasing, is that the product photos are a little misleading. Since the instructions say not to crowd the basket, you should expect to make less food at once than the pictures suggest.
I didn't believe people who said that they replaced their oven with an air fryer but in my household this is absolutely true. It also means not heating up our living space by running the oven which is a nice ancillary benefit during the warmer months. I'm delighted with this purchase - it's far exceeded my and my wife's expectations!

EPOS Impact 1061T ANC:  I was going to return these initially because out of the box these headphones were feeding me back my own voice in an unbelievably distracting way.  My own sibilance was particularly annoying, delayed and distorted.  This is how I fixed it:
1)  Download the EPOS app.
2)  Pair the headphones.
3)  Set Sidetone to 0% for both TalkThrough and ANC.  This is critical.  Without this, I would have returned the headphones because even 5% was too distracting.  Turn off Sidetone completely by setting it to 0%.  This is a setting for both ANC and TalkThrough.  Toggle between both and make sure they're both at 0.
If you want to hear your own voice, select TalkThrough.  This has the most natural feeling.  If you don't want to hear things around you, reduce the TalkThrough level from high to medium to low to see what works best.  If it's still too much background noise, turn on ANC.  While your own voice is muffled, the resonance in your own head will make up for it.  This is what I typically keep it on.  It actually helps me focus more on the person speaking this way.
Hopefully this helps anyone having this issue.  I called a few friends using these and mentioned I had a new headset, they said I sound clearer than if I were just using the phone.  I walked out near a busy street and they couldn't hear any outside noise.  I even put my head right near a speaker playing a voice only podcast very loud just to find out if it cancels out the sound for the recipient.  They couldn't hear a thing besides me.  Very impressive technology.  5 stars.
Side note, I got these "Open Box - Like New".  The look and function as new.  Saved a bunch going this way.

I got both the Knockbox and tampering station kit, seriously it makes your life SO much easier. I got their Tamper (58mm ) and distribution tool, scale and little triangular dosing cup. I also got Starbucks syrup (Carmel and vanilla to put at the bottom of the cup for a lattee ) and a couple of little glass espresso cups that look like tiny beakers so you can easily pour into your cup after. You’ll see in the picture. I’ve been making Lavazza Crema E Aroma Whole Bean Coffee Blend, 2.2-Pound Bag (8/10 strength) and it’s good and strong too… if you grind the beans on the finest setting it’ll clog the machine. I had it set to 5 and it works great. I usually scale out about 17 with the beans grind them and put them in a small tupper ware for each one so it makes the entire process so much easier because I’m on the go so much . Also makes it easy to just have it set up in the morning and just turn it on. The milk frother takes time and just make sure you purge it each time to clean and every time you turn on the machine have the knob in the middle  until all the settings light up that’s how you know it’s ready for water, steam , grinding , one or two shots. Sometimes it’ll need to reheat just put it back to the middle setting until it is ready again it doesn’t take long . When doing the milk , once all the lights are on turn to the steam button and just turn the handle to a 3 o’clock position with the milk . Just barely submerg it and when it bubbles submerge it and hold until you feel it’s just about too hot to hold and that’s how you know it’s done. I like to add a tiny bit of cinnamon on top! Hug win on this machine but prep items are key I think for any at home espresso making .

Anker Soundcore P30i buds.
First and foremost I want to be clear that I am rating these buds purely on their own merit.  Without their software, without any Equalizer, just on how they perform straight out of the box.
Baseus and Tozo and Jlabs are some of the names when we think of Budget Bass Buds.  And for those who are looking for good, clean bass... I'd compare these with Jlabs.  For bass, right out of the box, playing music with bass in it, they deliver a clear, audible thump, without the actual pounding vibration.  Right now, I'm listening to Cry Little Sister, from the Lost Boys soundtrack, at volume EIGHT.  (That's not even halfway up my volume bar from my phone).
And the base tune soundstage is really, really good.  Especially for a bass tuned base.  The vocals, and background vocals are right up front.  Crisp, clear, and don't sound like they are being overwhelmed by anything.  And I can definitely hear every hit from the bass drums, as well as count the cords on the keyboard.
Now I'm at 12, and those bass drums are starting to pound.  Other than it's significantly louder, I'm still hearing good clarity of the different ranges.  I can't say this for my Tozo T18 Crystal buds, without tuning.
My Baseus BP1 pros would be creeping over the midrange at this volume on the base tune.
Ok, now I'm at 18.  A lot louder than I usually listen to.  The highs are much more prominent over the lows.  Which is the opposite of how a lot of bass speakers work.
Honestly, this kind of division of the ranges from a single driver speaker is kind of surprising, especially at 20 to 25 dollars.
Battery life is good too.  I have a 10 hour day.  2 hours on the bus, 8 hour shift at work.  With the ANC turned on, they need a quick charge at lunch to carry me home.  With ANC turned off, yeah, I can get back in the door before they need to be charged.  Sometimes just barely, if I've had them cranked up.
ANC- on the bus they do pretty good.  Cuts down a lot of the engine and sound noise from the bus.  I can still hear people talking next to me, but at about half what it would be without the buds in.
At work?  Well it's so noisy at work even full blown ear muffs aren't making it good.
Feel- ok this is subjective, because my right ear canal is different from my left.  In my right, I can feel a bit of pressure when I put them in.  But once in, they're quite comfortable, and I can fall asleep with them in, as a side-sleeper.
Bluetooth is good.  Stays connected as long as I'm in range, and range is definitely acceptable.  Definitely better than the chap 17 dollar Onn buds I have.  Easy to pair also.
My only real complaint is no front panel to show the charge on the batteries.
All said the bass isn't as deep on the base soundstage as Tozo delivers, but it's cleaner.  Tozo also offers much better options in their software, as does Baseus, in some ways.
I DO like a lot that SoundCore went the route of making the stems wider, instead of longer.  Having long hair, it's less likely to get caught on the stems, and pull them out.
Speaking of pulling them out.  I decided to do some headbanging.  My glasses flew off but these buds didn't budge.
Overall though I have no regrets at all, buying these very good sounding set of inexpensive buds.

What’s wild is when you turn the noise canceling on, they shut all the mics off and it’s COMPLETELY quiet. I’ve never had ear buds that are THIS quiet and noise canceling. The first time I used this feature was in the gym while music inside was blaring. When I turned noise canceling on, I looked up and thought someone instantly cut the music off in the gym entirely cause I couldn’t hear any of it. It was like the power in the whole building went out it was so quiet. For the price of these, I’d say you can’t beat them.

Call quality... isn't this feature one of the most important components that will drive us towards or far away from a device...Yes!!!! So here it is: Shockingly amazing call quality. The case might actually be one of my favorite details. It’s compact enough to slip into a pocket or small section of my bag, protects the earbuds well, and the built-in phone stand is surprisingly handy. I initially thought that might be more of a novelty feature, but I’ve actually used it for hands-free viewing and really like having it built into something I’m already carrying.
I also love the color and overall design. Everything feels thoughtfully made, from the size and weight to the controls and Bluetooth connection. Pairing was quick, the connection has been reliable, and the earbuds feel like something I can comfortably use for hours rather than just short listening sessions.
This is also one of those products that has made me much more curious about the rest of Soundcore’s lineup. I’ve been impressed by how much performance and functionality Anker packed into such an affordable pair of earbuds, and now I’m especially interested in seeing how their higher-end headphones, newer audio products, and other Soundcore models compare. I ordered one of these after my place of employment got tired of keyboards failing constantly. After several months of outright abusive use by my co-workers, they still performed flawlessly with a lovely sense of tactile feedback, soda spills aside. One failed only after half a thermos of coffee was spilled into it, but that's to be expected from anything not waterproof rated.
After ordering one for myself to use at home, I LOVE typing on it. It's my first true mechanical keyboard, and it's pleasant to just tap away, typing whatever I feel like. Each key feels like it's got two levels of depression (almost like me): First a clear 'catch' when the key activates and types, and then another more firm one when you reach the bottom of the key well. I've yet to have it double-type anything even when my clumsy fingers wanted to, although it hasn't saved me from butterfingering my keystrokes in games.
As far as gaming goes, it's not PERFECT. It does make an audible noise when typing, so when you are frantically spamming the strafe or jump keys, it's going to sound like clicking the mouse over and over, but it's really no worse than your average mouse. If you're wearing headphones and blasting your speakers, you won't notice it. If you're in a silent small room, you can't avoid hearing it. Find your medium.
Its clearly more meant for office work, but I find it good for gaming, and it's sturdy and heavy enough it doesn't move around at all or feel like it'll die if I drop my phone on it.

Analyze this product review:

As my first mechanical keyboard, I was quite overwhelmed with choices of keyboards when looking to make my purchase.  I had seen several reviews of various keyboards and brands and found that Corsair had pretty consistently good reviews.  I saw they had just recently released the Vanguard 96 so I gave it a shot.  I'm glad I did!
I bought the one with linear switches, and they feel incredible to type on.  I was never convinced that I really wanted a mechanical keyboard until I felt how much better typing on linear switches feels, and now I'm not sure I could ever go back to a membrane keyboard.  The switches are smooth with no signs of wear after about four months of daily use.  I also never understood why so many keyboard reviews mentioned the sound the keys make when typing, but I can understand now.  It sounds great and isn't too loud at all.
The RGB backlighting on this keyboard is amazing.  I'm still not fully sold on kitting out my entire PC with RGB lighting, but this keyboard certainly makes me see the potential!  The colors can be adjusted keyboard-wide all the way down to a key-by-key level.  The animations are nice as well.  They keys light up evenly across the keyboard.  I haven't noticed any keys that are especially lighter or darker than the others.  They're pleasant to look at.  I think MAYBE the only complaint I have about the included keycaps would be that only the tops of them are shine-through, making the white key function markings on the front hard to see in the dark.  I think if the function symbols/marks on the front of the keys were shine-through as well, it'd make seeing them easier.  However, this is a very minor thing in my opinion.
The LCD screen is bright and vibrant.  It offers some relatively-useful options now that the keyboard has iCUE support (more on that in a moment).  I have the screen showing the currently playing Spotify song usually, but it can also display temps, fan speeds, memory usage, etc. as well as the time and date and other things.
I knowingly purchased the keyboard knowing it didn't have iCUE support at the time.  For the first three or so months, I used it with the Corsair Web Hub to keep it updated and change the settings.  It works well, though the customization is more limited when using it in the Web Hub, as you might expect.  The LCD screen has no useful widgets, instead only showing still images or animated GIFs in addition to the usual status indicators for things like CAPS Lock, polling rate, knob function, etc.
However, now Corsair has introduced iCUE support for the Vanguard 96, opening up a TON more customization options.  Being my first Corsair product, I was a little overwhelmed by just how much customizability was suddenly possible!  As this keyboard is still relatively new, there are some quirks regarding iCUE they're working on, but overall it's solid as it is.
The only real issue I've experienced with this keyboard is that key presses would fairly often register twice in quick succession, causing me to have to backspace quite a bit and fix the many double letters it would type.  I don't know if this is a common issue with mechanical keyboards, but I've read I'm not the only one having this issue with this particular keyboard.  Corsair have since introduced a "Debounce Time" setting in both Web Hub and iCUE.  I have configured mine with a debounce time of 3ms which has completely eliminated the problem.  It doesn't add any noticeable latency to keypresses when typing or gaming.  Because of this setting, I'm now completely happy with the purchase!
The included wrist rest feels absolutely amazing!  It's made of a soft, smooth material with ample padding underneath.  It attaches magnetically to the front of the keyboard, so it's extremely easy to remove when cleaning it.  I wish all keyboard wrist rests felt this good!
Overall, I love this keyboard.  I was able to get it on sale which made it an even better deal in my opinion.  After using standard-layout membrane keyboards my entire life, I'm still getting used to the 96% layout of the Corsair Vanguard 96, but it's a solid keyboard and I don't think I could ever go back to membranes!

I've spent enough time on a keyboard that this wasn't much of a problem (the characters are all paired and layed out in the standad way), but it was distracting at first.  Also distracting but not a big issue is that the highly stylized font used for the letters makes some of them difficult to read.
The big issue though is that, when typing rapidly, many of the keys - especially the E (most used letter in thee English language!) "bounce", creating TWO entries of the letter instead of just the one I intended.  This happens much more than occasionally - for example, I've already had to edit this paragraph several times to correct doubled charracters.  It makes head-down rapid typing - important to achieve "flow" - nearly impossible.
Since this makes the keyboard essentiall unusable for my purposes, I've had to downgrade it to just two stars - a very low rating from me.  I'll be selecting a different keyboard, and probably donating this one to Goodwill...

It wasn't that long ago that I didn't think I could live without a number pad and now I'm finding myself using 40% keyboards, but every so often it feels nice to go back to something that has a number row, function row, AND a number pad.
Before I get into the full review, let me just start with the part you really want to know about: the sound. The switches have a creamy, mid-toned clack to them and are not too loud for shared office environments, in my opinion. There is a little bit of scratchiness if you listen really closely, and if you remove them from the board and listen, you can hear it pretty clearly, but the soft keyboard plate material and all the foams really do a good job at dampening any kind of harsh or scratchy sounds overall. I included a video of some typing sounds on both an external mic and the camera mic so that you can get a sense of what this really sounds like. The external mic is a bit closer to how it sounds in real life, but it makes it sound a bit louder than what it actually is. With the configuration of the board, especially because it's plastic and has a bunch of foam in it, I do think you could pretty easily achieve a thocky build if you wanted to swap the switches for something deeper sounding.
Onto the other stuff:
This is essentially a 96% keyboard, so it has almost all of the keys you would find on a full-sized keyboard, except that it's missing the navigation cluster (prt scrn, scr lk, pause, insert, home, and, pg up, pg down) that would normally fall between the alphas and the number pad. Using those buttons has fallen out of favor with a lot of people, though if you do a lot of word processing or text entry, you may find that you need them a lot. This keyboard shines in that it actually has the layer 1 function buttons printed on the keycaps, so if you need those keys, you can find them easily, and they can be accessed by holding fn + whatever key you need the layer 1 functionality of. Having programmability by way of VIA means that you can customize they keys of this board to basically do whatever you want them to do. Want F5 down where Alt lives? You can have it. Want F2 instead of Caps Lock? Sure, go for it! Flashing the PCB with VIA compatibility is one of the very smart choices Kemove made when designing this board.
The keys themselves don't feel or look cheap, and are double shot, so there is no fear of the legends ever wearing off, even with years of use.
South-facing RGB is one of those non-negotiables in keyboards these days for those who are into RGB, so it is yet another great design choice that this board includes it. But Kemove made what I consider to be a really strange choice when they elected to build this with a PCB (the electrical circuit board that makes the keyboard work, and that switches plug in to) that only accepts 3-pin switches.
Nowadays, almost all switches, especially those that are made by the major manufacturers like Akko, Gateron, HMX, Keygeek, Wingtree and Bsun are 5-pin. That means that if you want to use any of those switches in this keyboard, you need to cut off the two plastic pins on the bottom of each switch (don't cut the metal pins or else the switches won't work anymore) with a pair of wire cutters/diagonal pliers or cuticle nippers before they can be inserted into this PCB. Thankfully, snipping those off doesn't render the switches useless in other boards that support 5 pins (they will also accept 3 pins), it will just offer a bit less stability if you want to use them in another keyboard going forward. Out of over a hundred keyboards in my collection, I have never come across a single one that only accepted 3-pin switches, so this feels like a bit of a miss for me.
If this were the only keyboard I were ever going to use, I would definitely not hesitate to buy some new switches that fit my desired sound profile to then lop off the plastic pins, but because I swap boards daily at the least, and several times per day at most (this is the 5th board I've used today), I wouldn't want to be modding switches in an irreparable way. That's a decision you'll have to make for yourself, though again, I really like the stock switches that come with this board, and I think they would appeal to the vast majority of people purchasing this board.
The screen is fine, though I find myself steering away from screens nowadays since they offer minimal utility and take up valuable keyboard space, but I do love me a knob. This knob has a nice tactile feel, and is auto-programmed to adjust the volume right out of the box. Pressing it brings up the various menu settings and lighting controls on the screen, which I did actually find to be the most useful function for the screen and a nice touch.
I absolutely hate the text they insisted on putting above the screen. "Keys never lie" is such a strange phrase and there is no need for it written on the board. I will probably see if I can take this off with a magic eraser. Other than that, there is no obnoxious branding anywhere on the case.
Dongle storage underneath the board has become fairly commonplace and I think it's smart placement.
I own one other Kemove mechanical board, and compared to this one, it's pretty janky. I think my original Kemove was like $30, sounded pretty horrible with cheap red switches, had very little customization options, and had north facing LEDs. So for an extra $50, you can get this board that offers the functionality of a dedicated number pad, a creamy sound signature, a screen for some cute gifs, a knob for easy volume control, and an overall build quality that blows that original Kemove board out of the water. They're stepping up their game, and I can't wait to see what they come out with next.

I love this keyboard. I have lots and lots of keyboards, many mechanical. I have not fell in love with a keyboard like this for a long time. So what do I love? First, the sound is pretty normal. It's not emitting a huge amount of mechanical clickety-clack noise. I really like the layout. I really like the color scheme, where you have an interesting quick grouping of keys by the coloring which is meant to be productive than say snazzy. The keycaps are very readable. It has a knob that by default deals with volume up/down/mute.
And a screen. I actually enjoy the screen. It's not just doing some random cute animation. It's working. I like looking down and seeing the date and time on the keyboard. I'm not a huge fan of seeing the key status (like caps lock) on the screen but it's something. I'd prefer more of an LED light on the individual key but this is better than nothing. It also shows if you're in Windows or MacOS mode.
Saying that: there's a switch for Windows and MacOS. There's a switch for wired, Bluetooth, and wireless. Yes, it has a wireless dongle with a great little home built into the bottom of the keyboard. Push on a little spot and it opens up so that you can pull the wireless dongle out and get to work. Great design.
When I was first using it, I have to admit for some reason the shift key wasn't getting held down enough so I had a lot of lower case letters sneak in. Also, the raised surfaces for the F and the J keys (so that you can home your fingers for the QWERTY layout) and pretty subtle compared to other keyboards.
Another criticism: I had to go to their web driver page for the keyboard in order to set the time for the keyboard. It was not too far off, but enough that the web app had to fix it. And yes, their web app allows ABUNDANT customization of the keyboard. And you can also customize some aspects just through the display screen w/out using the web app, so there's that. But if you can use the web app, use the web app.
But I started testing this and I just kept it plugged in and did several projects with it. I'm going to keep an eye on KEMOVE and see if they have an Alice layout next.
All in all: this is like the fifth keyboard I've tested in the past year and easily the top one.

But honestly, this KTC monitor impressed me for being a budget option at this price point so I’m going to go ahead and five my thoughts on it. packinng was what you would expect, nothing too fancy. Included was the mount and and stand for the monitor as well as the power cord, an HDMI cable and a DisplayPort cable.
The Good:
- Picture quality on this monitor is really good. 1440p looks crisp and clear and even downscaling to 1080p, while degrading the image a bit, still doesn’t look overly fuzzy. So if you really wanted to play or use this monitor at 1080p you could. (But being a 1440p monitor, don’t know why you would want to)
- there is very very little ghosting with this monitor at stock settings, i found that setting overdrive to low makes the ghosting pretty much go away without reducing image quality at all so that what I’ve kept mine on. I’ve attached a video to try and show an example of what it looks like.
- Freesync/ G-Sync works well without issues, there was no flickering at all during gaming at 165hz. Gaming felt smooth and i had no issues with stuttering or response time. Just note, 165hz only works with the DP cable. If you decide to use HDMI, you’ll only be able to go up to 144hz.
- Talking about the picture quality, the colors are vibrant without looking overly saturated, the blacks, while not being as dark as you’d see on a VA monitor, are still pretty good. Out of the box, you probably wont need to adjust the settings at all, unless you want really want to.
- Speaking of settings, i thought that using one button to essentially control everything would be annoying, but it’s actually pretty easy. Just press the button once to access the menu, and then move it in the direction you want to change whatever settings you want and then press the button again to turn off the menu.
The Bad:
- the monitor did arrive with some stuck pixels at the bottom right corner of the screen , just above the power button. It wasn’t enough to make me want to return it, as it isn’t noticeable when using the monitor for gaming or when using it for day to day tasks. This is more a QC issue more than anything, so your mileage may vary. I’ve attached a picture of it so you can see it for yourself.
- although it doesn’t affect performance at all, the RGB lights on the back of the monitor only have the option to turn it on or off and no setting to change the color to whatever you want. Out of the box, it just changes colors in this slow wave like effect. But this is just me being nit-picky.
- HDR on thins monitor is pretty bad, it does increase the brightness a bit if that’s what you’re looking for, but it washes out the colors too much and overall just looks too bright imo without manually changing settings in both the monitor and windows. If you’re looking for a monitor for primarily game in HDR, you might want to look at other options.
- this one is me being nit picky again, but the USB port on the back of the monitor doesn’t seem to have functionality, seems its just there to use a USB stick to update firmware or something. I plugged a mouse in there and a USB light strip, the mouse didn’t work at all and only half of the light strip lit up. So while a cool feature, doesn’t seem all that useful. I don’t know, maybe it’s in a firmware update that I haven’t done yet? Ill update this if i’m able to figure out more.
UPDATE: the USB port on the back works, i ended up swapping out old parts for new ones and it suddenly started working. I tried a LED strip and a mouse and both worked fine. I don’t know why or how this would interfere with the monitor, but it is what it is.
Overall, this monitor is really solid for the price, it comes with decent enough features to make it comparable with other options, but keep in mind it is a budget monitor so you won’t get some of the features here like you’d see with higher end models. But if you’re looking to get a gaming monitor with good image quality, good colors, high refresh rate, a 1ms response time and no ghosting, you’d be hard pressed to find a better monitor at this price point.

I did a lot of research before buying an air fryer, and this one was the best that I could find for the size and the price. I can tell you that it works very well for my needs. The size is roughly the same as a large microwave (although a bit taller), and it has a nice large area for cooking your meals. It cooks fast and has about as much noise as I'd expect from an air fryer (roughly the same amount of noise you'd have from a microwave). That being said, I have a few complaints that I'm not sure are related only to this model or not. The biggest one is the pre-heat feature on Air Fry mode. It does not pre-heat at all, so my first time trying to use that mode took a bit longer than usual because of how much colder air was inside the unit. I found that the best way to combat this is to start it on bake mode for the temperature you want, wait for it to preheat, and then stop it and switch it to air fry mode. Doing that keeps enjoy warmth inside that it keeps your cooking time about where the recipe indicates it should be. My next issue is the stupid alarm for when you should rotate your food to cook thoroughly. I don't know if this alarm is based on sensors, but the manual indicated that it's based on timing and should go off about halfway through your set cooking time. It doesn't. The stupid alarm sounds a random point, sometimes when there's 8 minutes left of a 22 minute cook time. I don't use it because I don't trust it. The unit also throws A LOT of heat behind it, so you want to keep it at least six inches away from any outlets (unless you want the outlet plates to melt). I was thankfully smart enough to do that but noticed it every time I went to unplug it (as I've read in some reviews the unit can turn itself on when not in use). Still, for the price and what it saves me in comparison to running my large electric range...I'm fairly happy with it. I use paper liners in it and the one tray as a drip pan so it keeps it very clean even when you're cooking some messy stuff. I use it pretty often, and I'm happy with it. I'm even happier that I didn't have to pay the $300 more to get the Ninja version (which, I discovered during my research, has a whole host of its own issues).

You can make 'Croutons' with the 'Toast' preset, but they're not as good as other preset options for that.
However, I did decide to keep this unit for the other types of things it does do very well.  By the way,
I tried 4 very similar units (other brands) and sent them all back.  Two of them actually died on me after a very short while.  This unit is still running and I use it many times each week.  I unplug it after each use.
Pros & Cons:
Pro's
- The Air-fry preset is really great.  It cooks fast and very well.  The best of my testing.  Chicken, especially,
was excellent.  Any kind of potato's.
- I like the fact that that the power does NOT turn off when the doors are opened.  Other units
you have to redo everything after you open the door/s.
- Dehydrate works well, although it's only useful for small batches.  The fan can't be adjusted, in this
mode, so if you're drying Parsley, or anything very lightweight, it will tend to blow all over the place...
Heat adjustment, in this mode, is pretty decent.
- Proof works well for all my dough's.  Max. Time is 2-hours/Max. heat is 95F.  I wouldn't mind having a
little more head-room/adjustment/override capability on this preset/mode.
- The grill actually works.  It does make nice grill-marks.  Some units I tested did not grill at all.  The lower
heating elements need to get red-hot, in order to grill properly.  This unit did well.
- The rotisserie works well, although the unit is a little bit too small for a large, whole chicken.
It's very tight.  You have to tie up the bird very carefully.  I don't use Mr. Lagasse's method, which is in
the user-manual, because it's not adequate.  I'd like to have a couple more inches of elbow-room, in all
directions.  Even better, if it would rotate a small-medium Turkey...  Like the old 'ShowTime' rotisserie's.
- The 'Bake' preset and all the other presets seem to work well.  Except for Toast.  But, they do have
unnecessary limits on Time, Temperature, Fan control, and burner control.
- Preheats very quickly.
- Not hard to clean. Just wipe it out with a towel while it's still a little bit warm.
Cons:
- The 30-second timer on the light button really bugs me.  The light should stay on until I turn it off.
- I don't like the logo-light staying on, if I want to leave the unit plugged in.  Waste of electricity.
The whole unit should power-off and not consume any electricity when turned off.
- Some of the presets are too restrictive for control over Time, Heat-level, Fan & Burners...
It would be nice to have full override control on most of the presets...
- Not big enough to do a Turkey on the rotisserie/spit.  And just barley big enough for a large Chicken (on
the spit).  The pans and rack capacities are small.  Good for one or two people only.
- The spit bar assembly is not the best I've ever used.  If this was my company/unit, I would redesign it.
And part of the problem is also the fact that there is very little elbow-room to work with, so you have to
get the spit set in the meat, just right...  It can be tricky...
Tips:
- I put Aluminum-foil on the bottom drip-tray, and keep it like that all the time.
- Try not to get any fat or food on the burners.  Bottom burners are mostly the ones you need to be
concerned with.

I really wanted to like this chair but, while there are things I do like about it, there are too many things I find fault with.
For context, I am 73 years old, am 6’3” and weigh in around 265lbs. My last chair was designed for big and tall people and it fit me to a tee. I worked from home for two years during the apocalypse and that chair was super comfortable and I could spend over 8 hours a day in it with no problems. Unfortunately the faux leather wore off so I needed a replacement. I retired a couple of years ago and now only spend a few hours a week in front of the computer so I really don’t need anything too fancy or expensive.
After researching a bunch of chairs, I settled on the Tralt Mesh Back Ergonomic Computer / Gamer Chair. I’ve never had a mesh chair before so I expected it to feel a lot different from my old all faux leather chair and it does feel a lot different but it’s what I expected.
The good:
1. Price. For $130.00, I think this is a pretty good deal.
2. Assembly. Fairly quick. It took me about 30 minutes to unbox and assemble but I took my time so you could probably do it in 15-20 minutes easy. All parts lined up correctly and all bolts screwed in without any problems.
3. Weight. This chair is at least 50% lighter than my old chair so carrying it fully assembled upstairs was easy for me.
4. Appearance. Very nice.
5. Adjustments. Raising and lowering the chair is smooth and easy. Control lever and hydraulic piston work well. Tilting mechanism is also smooth and easy.
The not so good.
1. IMO, this chair is NOT for anyone over 6’ if you are going to spend any time in it. The Amazon description says this will fit people who are 5’2” - 6’4”. Nope. The measurements shown in the description PHOTOS says 5’3” - 6’2”. Also nope. The front of the seat cushion hits my legs about half way up the thigh. It should hit closer to the knees. This makes me feel like I’m sitting on the edge of the chair. If the seat cushion was 24” in depth instead of 19-1/2” this would solve that problem. Also, if the lumbar support was positioned correctly, it might fit and feel better as well.
2. Lumbar support. As other reviewers have stated, the lumbar is too low and hits your tailbone, not the lumbar area of your back. This setup might be acceptable for someone shorter but for anyone 6’ or taller this is a problem. The lumbar is adjustable but it’s kind of a moot point in my case.
3. Arm rests. They are adjustable and slide forward but for taller people, even if fully adjusted forward, the arm rests still sit too far back and are not comfortable.
4. Stability. When I sit in the chair it doesn’t feel super solid. I don’t know how to explain it but I feel like I am going to tilt off to the side. It’s just a weird feeling. The chair doesn’t actually tip side to side but it’s just this odd feeling I get when I sit and even when rolling forward.
5. Weight capacity. The description says the chair has a weight capacity of 330lbs. This is probably true but, after using the chair for a while, I wonder about the longevity of the chair for someone heavier like me.
Look, as I said earlier, for the price this is a good deal. I only use the chair once or twice a week so decided to keep it as returning it was more of a problem than I wanted to deal with. If the seat cushion was 3-4” longer, it would fit my legs much better and I would be a lot happier.
My advise: if you are big and tall like me, pass on this chair. Spend a little more money and get something that fits you.

Analyze this product review:

It's extremely rare that I give out a 5 star review for a tech product of any kind, but I honestly, trying to nitpick these would be reaching. Like. My only gripe is I wish the little charging case had a small hole on it to loop a Keychain through for easier carrying. Beyond that, these are the best earbuds I've personally owned.
Let me put it in perspective with a breakdown of the issues I've had with ear buds over the years:
I have sensory issues and am extremely sensitive to pressure on my ears/head. I can't wear over ear headphones without getting headaches. Ear buds I can tolerate much better but I have spent over a decade trying to find an ear bud that didn't just start slipping out of my ear or that wouldn't make my ears sore over time. My ears canal isn't exceptionally tiny but my outer ear is quite small and most ear buds simply didn't work. They were the wrong shape or just too large to fit in the ear opening and stay put unless I crammed them into my ear canal.
But that doesn't work long term. Inevitably, I had to push the earbud back into place. Back in the days of wired buds this was a tolerable inconvenience. I was fine with that. I rocked the first Gen Bluetooth Bose ear buds, the ones connected by a wire to each other, for a couple years and they were tolerable but still constantly popped out of my ears.
When true wireless came out having to adjust and push ear buds back in my ears became an intolerable frustration. I was constantly tripping the touch controls no matter how careful I was, and when you have to push earbuds back into place ever 15 to 20 minutes and you're pausing your music or accidentally hanging up on a call, it makes the buds feel pointless to have.
I've tried pixel buds, JBL, skull candy, beats, Sony, JLab, on and on and none of them ever fit right. They were all slipping out no matter what I did and they inevitable made my ears hurt within an hour of wear.
These don't do that. I can run on the treadmill, clean my house, do yoga, dance around, act a fool and these buds stay in place comfortably for hours. If I do need to make a minor readjustment, the physical click button on the stem means I don't accidentally pause my music or audio book anymore, and when I need to, it's a reliable, easy single click on the stem to adjust the noise canceling or pause my audio.
The fact that the button is a physical one and has a nice little click to it is so satisfying. I miss fiddly technology. Stuff with buttons and dials. In a world full of Everything is Touch Navigated Now, a single clickable button is such a nice return to form.
The form factor of these buds is lightweight, comfortable, and for the first time ever I don't feel like I'm fighting my headphones.
The next thing is sound quality. I am kind of picky about sound quality and clarity. These things sound amazing. The equalizer that you can use in the app makes tweaking them to exactly what I want so easy. On top of that, the ANC has its own adjustability to filter high, mid, or low frequency noise, as well as an adaptive setting to suit my needs for any environment. The transparency mode isn't full of that scratchy noise I have come to expect from earbuds. It's crisp and clear with a very subtly, soft white noise that is actually pretty great for when I just need to combat my tinnitus but stay aware of my kiddo running around.
The app has a lot of great features, including a find my buds feature if you should lose track of one or both of them, and that's minor gripe number 2. It'd be great if there was a find my buds feature for the charging case itself in case I misplace the whole thing, but having some kind of device location at all is still nice and not a necessity, just a perk.
These headphones charge quickly and I've honestly never been in a situation where the headphones have died on me when I've been using them. The battery life is solid I've used them with ANC on for 3 to 4 hours at a time. The app gives you a readout of the individual batter life of each headphone so you know at a glance when you're getting low, but I've yet to have them dip below 25% during heavy use.
The case charges by usb c, which is nice. It charges pretty quickly, too.
I liked these so much I bought a pair for my girlfriend who is equally sensitive and has had the same issues as I have with ear buds in the past. She lives in noise canceling buds to help her focus and avoid overstimulation and she too, agrees that these are so comfortable and fit so well that she forgets they're in sometimes.
All in all, I've never had any issues with connectivity or sound quality, they sound great, fit great, have great features, and at under $100 they are a great deal. My Samsung buds cost twice that and I hated them. These are excellent. Absolutely recommend.

Great Bluetooth earphones! If you are looking for comfortable fit, great sound quality, and good mic for calls this is the pair for you.
I have had my eyes on these earphones for a while and bought them when they were one sale. Totally worth it!
The quality of these are great. They sound great right out of the box, hardly had to mess with any of the EQ settings in the app. So it was surprising just how well everything sounded once I started using them.
More Thoughts:
I'm not a professional audio reviewer or hardcore audiophile, so this is just coming from an high quality audio enjoyer. I will also have some comparisons to the Jabra Elite 7 Pros that I've used.
Sound Quality:
I really love the sound of the Nothing Earphones, music sounds bass-y and punchy, if you listen to rock or music with a deeper or more intense sound, these handle that great. I listen to a lot of different genres and all of them sound really clear and balanced without touching the EQ settings. I haven't messed with them a lot myself but you have a couple presets and the ability to set your own. Personally I haven't felt the need to since the sound is so high quality and clear to start with. If you like to listen to your music loud they handle them easily without making your ears or head hurt. Definitely my favorite sounding pair of earphones I have experienced.
Mic quality:
I used a pair of Jabra Elite 7 Pros for over 2 years as my daily earphones for music and videos that were priced at $140 USD when I first purchased them that were great but after two years they needed an upgrade. A complaint I always had with the Jabras was the mic quality for calls, my voice was always too low or muffled, but with the Nothing earphones my voice is so much clearer and I have even had people comment how loud I sound using them! So they are great for calls. On the receiving end voice you are are really clear with hardly any background noise coming through.
ANC (Active Noise Canceling):
The ANC on the Nothing Earphones are fantastic. In the app there are a few different options: low, medium, high, and adaptive. The default is high, and it makes it feel like you are in your own world. Once you are playing music or a video almost all the outside noise disappears. I work in an office at a marine so sometimes voices or heavy machinery comes through but at such a low volume you hardly register it. Though I might have to give the edge to my Jabras with just how much more consistent the ANC is on them especially when you have a good fit. Great ANC but not best out there.
Transparency:
The transparency mode is not as good as the Jabra, I find that any music you may be playing can drown out any noise or voices you want to come through. It, in my opinion, doesn't let enough sounds through when you are at medium volume or louder especially if you find yourself talking a lot with them in. So if what you are playing isn't too loud its fine.
Controls/Buttons:
The buttons on the stems of the earphones function off of pinches, it is not your typical press or touch buttons. It takes a bit to get used to especially if you are used to a tactile press button like on Jabra products. But the accuracy of the pinches/controls is great. I haven't had it do something I didn't intended. Also the range of custom options for the buttons is great with you being able to change them to whatever scheme you want. The only thing you can't change is the Play/pause button. But I was happy to be able to change the buttons functions to what I needed them to be, which a bit more than I could say for the Jabras.
Fit:
The ear tips that the Nothing earphones come with are very comfortable and fit really nicely. I typically use the smallest tips that an earphone comes with, anything bigger usually falls out or pushes itself out of my ear, but the medium size that comes on them fit surprisingly great for me. I did switch to the smaller ones for comfort but I can't complain about the larger size. You get three sizes with these earphones: small, medium, and large. The material feels really nice in the ear  as well. And the overall shape of the earphones feels great in the ear, just sits comfortable inside, sometimes I can forget they are even there, and the stems are no bother.
Battery/Charging:
The case and the earphones charge really fast and the indicator light on the case is nice way to tell the charge level. They come with a very short usb-c to usb-c cable that charges the case so quickly, especially with the right adapter. Charge much faster than the Jabra case and earphones. The battery life on the Nothing earphones is pretty great for 8 hour work days. And the case charge lasts me an entire week or more. If you are using the ANC or Transparency modes it does tank the life quite a bit, as with most earphones. The most I have had them last while using ANC on High nonstop is about 5 hours, which to me is pretty good. And once you put them in the case to charge you can definitely get an entire day out of them using ANC. Without ANC you can go through most of a day, maybe 10-12 hours or more of use. My jabras perform quite identically but the charge on them doesn't last as long after in the case for 10 minutes.
Conclusion:
There are probably things I've missed or things other people notice, but to the average person these earphones come at a great price and provide you with insanely great quality across the board. The mic alone makes this a worth while purchase. But the sound is smooth, crispy, and clear when you need it to be. My favorite set of earphones I've bought myself so far. They are definitely my go to daily drivers.

Instead of showing time, date, steps, calories, etc. all together, it only allows you to display one or two items. In my case, I could only show the time and date, which was disappointing.
Cons:
The app is probably the weakest part of this product. There’s a “Find My Phone” feature, but it disconnects every few minutes. You have to reopen the app to reconnect before using it again, which defeats the purpose - especially if you’re trying to locate your phone when it’s lost. Not sure how someone is supposed to find their lost phone but need their phone and watch need to be connected to the app before using this tool. Make it make sense??? You can’t lol.
It also claims to support notifications from apps like Snapchat, Facebook, and Instagram, but despite enabling everything, I haven’t received any of those. Not a single one. I only get basic notifications like calls, texts, and a few random apps.
I work in software, so I’m prettyyyy comfortable with tech. If I’m having trouble getting these features to work properly, that’s something to keep in mind if those functions are important to you. Please be aware of this if you’re searching for a watch solely for this reasoning.
Another downside is that the wristbands aren’t interchangeable - there’s no easy way to swap them out, which is limiting. Which really sucks.
Overall, for $50, it’s decent. But honestly, for an extra $20–$30, you could probably find something much better without all the disconnection issues this one constantly gives you.
I’ll give it a few more days before deciding whether to keep it or return it. More than likely I’ll be returning to get something more reliable but I’m writing this review for those who wants to stay in a reasonable price range, while giving them the honest review they deserve before spending their hard earned money.
Hope this helps!!
EDIT 5/24/26: I ended up keeping the watch. The more I used it, the more features I was discovering both in-watch, and in-app. However, I’m still keeping it as 3 stars because of the Cons I’ve listed still being an issue. I’d say give it a try yourselves and see how you like it. You can read all the reviews but it’ll affect everyone differently.

I own the newest Klein buds, Axil Xcor s and these too. Got these Disrupters for $144, I got the Kleins for $159 and the Xcores at $180 for President's Day sale. These are the most tech savvy but you have to use the app to get the most out of these earbuds. You can do the minimal without using the Walker app for which I've had zero issues with. Good phone call quality. The earbuds for whatever reason they're not 100% when case might be but not a biggie but I think once or twice I've had one ear bud dead  when case wasn't but that could've been on me. Nice size case. These by far sound the best and the loudest. Changing what frequency you hear is kind of cool depending on what environment you are using them in so these will be my casual and hunting buds. The dual case setup is clutch too. And the earbuds are always 100% fully charged. Sadly the sound is the worst out of all three and pretty quiet on phone call makes hearing the other person but they have the best noise reduction rating of 29. These will block out all noise above 85 decibels so it just is a blank cutoff of noise. So they will be my shooting buds. At the price I bought them for I'd probably get them again but not for $300.  The Kleins are the middle of the road buds. They sound pretty good all around. Easy to operate with Bluetooth on the left earbud, Smart Sense on the right bud. They're fast at connecting never had an issue with them charging either. Good phone call quality. Their case is the biggest but for work it helps stick in my occidental bags. Middle of the pack for being comfy of the 3. Easy in and out due to they kick out they have but it's a con if you end up using them with a beanie they will push on your ear and make them not comfy. Kleins will be the pair I use at work throwing up steel. At reg price $179 I would purchase them again. Each have their pros and cons but depending on what you'll use em for is the deciding factor imo.

The AOC 27 Inch QHD Gaming Monitor 240Hz 0.3ms has been fantastic so far. Before buying it, I had never owned a monitor above 60Hz, so I honestly didn’t think I would notice much of a difference. At first, I was a little skeptical because some reviews mentioned that the blacks were not very deep and that some units arrived with dead pixels or lines on the screen. However, my personal experience has been excellent.
My monitor arrived in perfect condition with no damage, dead pixels, or display issues, and the setup process was very simple. When I first started using it, I couldn’t immediately tell the difference between 60Hz and 240Hz. But after moving my mouse around and comparing it to my old monitor, the difference became very noticeable. The smoothness is honestly amazing.
The monitor also includes a lot of useful and fun features. It has a sniper mode, a built-in crosshair option that places a dot in the center of the screen, and even a timer feature. Another great feature is the ability to overclock the monitor up to 260Hz. There are also many ways to customize the display colors, including detailed manual adjustments.
One small downside is that the stand is not very adjustable. However, if adjustability is important to you, a monitor mount would work great with this setup and would easily solve that issue.
One thing I was initially worried about was the HDR performance because some reviews said it was not “true HDR.” In my experience, though, that concern ended up being overrated. The colors look vibrant and impressive, and overall the display quality has exceeded my expectations.
If you’re looking for an affordable 1440p gaming monitor with a high refresh rate and plenty of features, this is definitely a great choice.

If you are interested in transitioning from an old school to mechanical keyboard, want something with an absolutely sick looking design, is simple to use, and doesn't have insanely loud key press noises, this is definitely a top option! I have had this unboxed for barely 30 minutes and am already in love with it. It was super easy to plug-n-play and use the built in functions immediately.
I have used old style, full-length keyboards for decades and was extremely hesitant to try out a mechanical keyboard, especially because of the noise I had heard from seeing video reviews and how unsure I was if I could deal with the loss of full buttonology. One major reason I looked into one of this type/size was that I realized one of the main reasons I have issues with soreness and pain in my left shoulder, neck, and upper arm is due to how I would position my left hand and tilt the keyboard in order to use the traditional movement keys WASX on a full sized keyboard for gaming. With this one, my arm is now in a natural resting position at 90 degrees against my side, negating the angular stress on all those muscle groups, and when I want to do some typing while gaming, I don't have to stretch across the board to my left as much with my right hand to get to home keys.
Additionally, one big assumption killer was that, even though the size is cut down by a ton from a full-sized keyboard, the muscle memory transition to the slightly more compacted keys took hardly any time at all when typing with home keys. I type about 100 WPM, so I assumed I'd have a super difficult time with this aspect of the transition, but the spacing of keys doesn't have a huge difference of feel. The other big plus is that the noise level isn't huge on key press when gaming, and is not bothersome when typing; it's not that high pitched clickity clack you might get from many other types, rather a dull, thud-like sound.
Now add in the amazing painted design (especially if you like Japanese wood block print/art), and the colored light functions, which mind you are accessible by using the keyboard and the built in mini screen aka not requiring you to download software, as well as the pre-programmed FN + <key> functions that replace the buttons you lost from a full sized keyboard, and this thing is just a dream.
HIGHLY RECOMMEND to one and all, especially old folks like me that are afraid to make that leap into transitioning to a mechanical style board.
P.S.: If you're looking for actual dimensions of the keyboard itself, which are not on this Amazon page nor on the company's item page, they are approximately as follows: 12.75"x5.75"x1.375"-0.875" (the last number is the height, without the height extenders being used, at the top of the keyboard vs. at the bottom. it slopes upward towards the back)

The "meh" are the screen (which really doesn't serve any purpose). You can put GIFs on it if you like. It otherwise just shows the settings, but that's not necessary either. The software to power the LEDs is also rather lackluster and I would have preferred compatibility with SignalRGB or the like.
Now for the big con: south-facing LEDs. I don't know who ever thought this was a good idea, but all they do is blind the user and make any kind of glowing legends useless. It doesn't matter what kind of lighting you use with it if it's just shining directly at your face from the bottom of the keys. I still use the keyboard for all the good qualities, but am looking for something to replace it. In the meantime I have disabled the RGB, which just means it's going to waste. If you're a touch-typist or have a very well-lit desk, you'll likely be okay with it. I've also seen some people say there are ways to put tape on it to help with that, and I may have to resort to that, and again it seems like a problem that didn't need to exist in the first place.
But since everything else about the keyboard is so good, I'll give it 4 stars.

I purchased this air fryer convection oven after running into some limitations with the air fryer lid that I was using with my Instant Pot. Most notably that in order to make sure food was evenly cooked you had to remove the entire top and then take the pot out to shake/toss the food to make sure it was flipped. This is not an issue with this air fryer with the various foods I have tried so far with this particular unit. Even if I do have to flip the food over it's much easier to open up the door and pull out the tray to flip the food than I previously had to deal with the Instant Pot. The unit warms up quickly and cooks pretty much everything I've thrown at it evenly in a reasonable amount of time. I've cooked fish, bacon, french fries, chicken breasts, hamburgers,  and more without issue. The presets generally work well for the foods that they cover, some do require tweaking depending on the portion size you're putting in but that's to be expected. I haven't used the rotisserie function yet but I look forward to using it as there are several dishes that work better when rotisserie is an option. The light in the unit is a nice  extra to have to check on the food as it's cooking. To address some of the issues that I've seen brought up in other reviews:
* The trays that the unit comes with are a relatively fine mesh. I've seen some purchasers stating that they were rather sharp. The trays that I received with the unit are not sharp in the slightest and clean very easily with just a bit of soap and water.
* Some users stated that there was an odd smell when the unit was in use. I ran the unit for 15 minutes at 400 degrees as instructed when I first received the unit. That was the only time I detected a very faint chemical smell. I have not detected any smells coming from the unit other than the food I'm cooking.
* I have not had any shutdown issues with this unit at all. The unit is roughly 1 foot away from the wall on the counter it's sitting on and that seems to be more than enough clearance for heat to escape
If you're looking for an air fryer/convection oven that doesn't take up a lot of space but fits a surprisingly large amount of food in it this one is definitely worth considering.

Ok. So I'm a gamer/streamer. I wanted a nice gaming chair, nice within reason. I selected this one based off of the ratings and the amount of reviews it had. Let me preface this review by stating I am a disabled chubby woman lol. I'm 5'5 and 200 lbs so my review is for someone of that stature and support needs.
To start the ship time was estimated at nearly one month. Which was shocking to me, but it did arrive very early at only 9 days. (This was due to my proximity to one of their warehouses, I'm an hour from one of their 4 warehouses. So I can't assume this shipping time is the norm.) The box arrived in good condition, although massive and heavy.
Assembly was shockingly easy, the instructions were clear and all the parts were accounted for and they also send some extra bolts just in case, which is always nice.
Once assembled I put on the support pillows, the lumbar one was too large and firm for me due to my back issues. If the lumbar one was the same softness as the neck pillow I believe that would have been perfect.
The chair is nice quality, no scratches, dings, dents, or tears were evident after assembly. The material feels luxurious without the price tag. The chair is also completely gorgeous. I LOVE the dark purple color, all the other purples in chairs looked more pink, this is deep purple and lovely.
Now the downside. For this price I would have thought the chair would have been more comfortable. The curves on the lower part of the backrest are fairly protruding, if you aren't a small or average hipped person these press into your hips/bum. The seat itself feels extremely hard and flat, and feels as if it's tipping forward. For this price I just really was expecting at least some comfort and cushion and the cardboard box I think would be more cushiony. The armrests are constantly out of place, I think I spent more time adjusting them back to where they belonged. If the chair was priced closer to 130 I think I would be happy with it, but at this price point it is at I just expect better. My end result is selling the chair and I went and bought a nice executive office chair from an office supply store, where I could sit in the chairs first. That would be my suggestion, go sit in things before spending any money so you know what matters to you and what you like.
TL:DR Gorgeous chair, easy assembly. If you are anything other than standard sizes this chair might be a bit small. Chair lacks comfort and cushioning, wiggly armrests. Getting rid of my Gtracing chair and bought a nice office chair instead. (Writing this from the office chair and I have a happy bum.)
Good luck and happy gaming!

I've had this keyboard now over a year, having purchased it in April of 2025 (Review written in August of 2026).
I've had virtually zero issues with this keyboard, I work daily on my computer for hours at a time and have likely logged close to 8-10 million keystrokes on select keys. All of the keys from the factory still function well and I have not modified or changed anything with the keyboard.
The included dongle works well, I recommend the 2.4ghz mode as opposed to Bluetooth for decreased latency and range, although the Bluetooth functionality works well within a room. The battery life meets the companies claims, and charges within that spec as well. I recommend keeping some kind of type-c cable nearby to charge it, either directly from your computer or a wall-outlet.
Typing on this is great, I can type at roughly 98 wpm consistently on this keyboard at roughly 97% accuracy. I find the typing experience to be enjoyable, but light. The keys have a marble-like sound to them, and are soft and easy to actuate. The travel time is fairly generous, but soft, if you have a propensity to "fat finger" keys you'll more than likely have some accidental presses if you rest your finger on certain keys. This tends to happen less with general typing and more when resting my fingers of the WASD keys as I play games often.
For gaming I think this is great, but keep in mind that certain games require more keys (Star Citizen, Arma, or other complex sim style games). You will be making a sacrifice going with a 75% keyboard on accessibility. However for competitive titles, or most general games, this keyboard is a great addition. In games like Counter-Strike 2, Rematch, and Battlefield 6 I've been able to maintain my K/D and win percentages having come from a wired gaming keyboard previously. The included function keys are nice as well, which you can use to rebind or bind certain actions with if you're into that degree of customization. I've used this to extend the keyboard a bit having given up the keypad and other function keys.
The design and build quality are good as well, I've dropped this keyboard twice during cleaning and noticed no visible damage from both 3-foot falls. Cleaning is simple as well, the included key-stripper is easy to use and pops the key-caps out without much issue.
If you're into customization, you can replace the key-caps to your liking. I've recommended this to a friend who swapped his key-caps with metal ones, to which he's enjoyed. I prefer the feel and texture of the included keys. The plastic is generally strong and not-flexible, you won't notice any "deck" flex when pressing on the keyboard. The volume knob is a surprisingly nice feature, which you can turn to raise / lower the volume, as well as being able to push the dial in to mute / unmute. The included RGB lighting is bright and easy to read.
The only pain point is sometimes the receiver will kick out, which has happened more than a handful of times across the year and some change I've owned this keyboard. Frankly the fix is simple, switching the keyboard on and off resolved the problem immediately.
I think for the value this is a steal, I've recommended this keyboard to just about everybody and will stick with both the brand moving forward.

What I like most is the feel of the keys when typing and the sound. It has that characteristic mechanical keyboard sound that is very satisfying without becoming annoying when I’m working for several hours. I also think the 75% size is perfect: it takes up much less space on my desk without sacrificing the keys I actually use.
I also really like the way it looks. It feels stylish, solid, and much more polished than I expected. The wireless connection has worked very well, and being able to switch between devices is really convenient.
I mainly use it for work and do a lot of typing, so it was important to me that it be comfortable as well as nice-looking, and so far it has completely met my expectations.
When I bought it, I didn’t realize that the letters were printed on the front of the keycaps rather than on top. It only took me a few hours to get used to it, though, and now I actually like it because I think the lettering may wear off more slowly.
The only thing I didn’t like is that it doesn’t have a dedicated “Home” key. It has an “End” key, but not “Home.” That said, the software makes it incredibly easy to remap keys and customize their functions, so it works perfectly for me anyway.
I also like that you can choose from several colorful lighting effects, although I usually keep the lights turned off because I find them a little distracting while working. The keyboard is somewhat heavy, so I would consider it more of a desk keyboard than something you would want to carry around, which is completely fine for my use.

I got this during prime day so I paid less than 70 bucks for it and it is probably worth over $100. I am very satisfied with this purchase.
I originally bought it for my work computer but I was torn because it didn't come with the numbers pad And I use the numbers pad heavily for my job, but I was so attracted to the keyboard I ended up purchasing it anyway with a spare generic numbers pad which was a great investment.
Then I realized it had multiple inputs. It is Bluetooth, It is wired, and it has a wireless dongle and so I said to myself, "hey I can plug this in both my work PC and my personal PC!" So I use the cord for my personal PC and the dongle for my work PC and all I have to do is flip the switch on the back of the keyboard to toggle between modes. It cleared up the clutter on my desk because I no longer have two keyboards for both my PCs.
I'm a writer so I'm very attracted to the creamy sound and I added a video of one solid minute of me writing. I'm not pressing random buttons I'm actually typing in a word document lol.
The appearance is very sleek I am very fond of the front facing letters and I don't have to worry about them getting worn out the more I use it.
So far the quality and performance is great I will say with the dongle there's like a very very slight delay in terms of copying and pasting which is why I put the dongle into my work PC because I am also a gamer and I can't have the delay. So far I've played several games of OverWatch and have not had an issue with either the dongle or the wired connection in my personal PC because I originally did it with the dongle. So if you prefer to have the dongle in your gaming PC, you won't have any issues with delay.
It's about as heavy as a regular cherry keyboard. me personally I like the weight to it. I keep my gaming mouse weighted as well but that's just me.
I like the versatile knob on the right hand corner of the keyboard. It changes the modes of the lights on the keys and if you press and hold it it will change to volume So that was super convenient.
I read another review that said the driver's contained malware so I was a little wary to download them however with all of the modes that the lights have, I don't believe I'll need to download anything for this keyboard.
So far it's a solid five stars!!! Although I've only had it for a few days so if I run into any issues I will come back and update the review ☺️

I'm impressed. Coming from a 4 year old Corsair mechanical keyboard with cherry mx switches, I had high hopes that this keyboard would get the job done. It lacks dedicated media keys, but you still have media keys by using the function key.
The battery is excellent to start; I hope it lasts just as long as my Corsair did. The weight is a little beefy despite it being mostly plastic and thicc. The size is perfect if you intend to use it on your lap or TV tray. There are many different LED modes as well, which is nice, as well as the fact that you can set these modes without having to install some sort of app to control them.
While I primarily use the 2.4 connection, I do like the fact that it supports 3 bt devices. The response rate is very good and on par with the Corsair. You will have to get used to the arrow key layout with end, pg up, pg dn, and delete being in one single vertical row.
Probably the most intriguing thing that made me want to even look at it was the front etched keys, which were perfect for my use case. I usually rest the keyboard on a shelf slightly higher than my shoulder when I sit so the keyboard is closer to my eye level than my hands. These keys make it easier to quickly see and press some custom commands I have instead of having to pick up the keyboard, sit it on my lap or tray, and then use my commands.
The key presses are also very muted from the cherry mx switches, which is a plus and slightly more satisfying.
Overall, I'm Impressed.
(update as of 3-15-26)
Nearly a year later, the battery's lifespan has decreased to about 50% of its original capacity.

Here are my comments and concerns with model YX001 only.  The instructions have a few issues imho: black letters/words printed on a dark/darker background, I literally could not read them at times and had to go to another room with a spotlight to make sure I followed directions.  A box around the words are fine, but not a colored box.  The 6 star gear shims (piece I) on the arms really needs a better way to identify instead of “placed in the direction of the instructions”.  I am not having any issues with the arms so I assume I may have gotten it right.  There aren't any instructions when to tighten all the screws that you were told to leave untightened, that could lead to an issue if when you finally get the chair finished and see step 8 saying Done and try to sit in it.  Not impossible use the included Allen wrench (great it is included!) to tighten the screws from step 4 to Done because the T-handle will not fit in the now put together space.  We have a bunch of regular Allen wrenches so I was able to complete the tightening required.  Overall assembly was not that difficult and the time to accomplish it was not longer than expected.  While the above caused some delay, the chair is still fine after 4 weeks of continuous use.
The chair itself: the lumbar support is very nice and easy to adjust.  The arms are attached to the back and the seat seemingly to give more support for them when getting in and out of the chair.  The arms lifting up and away is nice.  The seat, after a couple of weeks, seems reasonable, not too soft or too hard, the mesh back is nice, and the gas lift feels and sounds solid.  The chair would be worth 4.5 Amazon stars, except…  I’ve had a lot of office chairs (including work) over my 50+ years of sitting in front of a computer daily: cheap chairs, relatively expensive, and in between.  I have a glass floor mat and the chair does not roll freely.  There are flat spots on the wheels and it takes effort to get the chair to start to roll anywhere on my mat while sitting in it.  The description says they are soft to reduce noise and they do on my mat.  When on glass all chairs still make a noise due to the nature of the mat, so that’s not an issue.  Compared to the rest of the chair the wheels aren’t up to what I expected and I am concerned about their longevity being soft with a non-circular shape.  Perhaps on carpeted floors this might be hidden.  Lastly, be aware the description says Lifetime Warranty, however an included index card says 5 years IF you send them an email, which I did, but was ignored for a couple weeks.  Only after using Amazon to complain about them were my inquiries finally answered.  It is indeed only 5 years (NOT lifetime) which is still a decent amount of years for a chair.  I will update this if any issues appear within 5 years.

I am actually amazed that a chair with ratings like this could be so uncomfortable. I never even considered an office chair could be uncomfortable until sitting in this one. Where do I start..
For reference I'm 5'7, 165lb. Should be pretty standard dimensions for the average office chair.

The max seat height is too low for a standard ~30" desk, forcing my elbows below the desk edge and my wrists at a bad angle. I mean come on.
